articles.title: Investidor do Feira FC tem nome retirado de investigação sobre apostas | G1
articles.standfirst: Bruno Karttos foi alvo de uma ação judicial no dia 13 de agosto, durante a Operação Aposta Suja deflagrada pelo Ministério Público da Bahia e do Rio de Janeiro.
articles.summary: Bruno Karttos foi alvo de uma ação judicial no dia 13 de agosto, durante a Operação Aposta Suja deflagrada pelo Ministério Público da Bahia e do Rio de Janeiro.
articles.body:
O empresário e investidor do Feira Futebol Clube, Bruno Karttos, teve o nome retirado da investigação do Ministério Público da Bahia, que apura a atuação de uma organização criminosa suspeita de explorar ilegalmente apostas online, aplicar golpes contra apostadores e lavar dinheiro.

Segundo informações apuradas pela TV Subaé, a investigação identificou que ele não tem nenhuma ligação com a empresa investigada pelo MP-BA. A mudança aconteceu após a análise de documentos apresentados pela defesa do empresário, que indicam outro homem como sócio e administrador da empresa investigada.

Um mandado de busca e apreensão chegou a ser cumprido na residência do empresário, que fica em um condomínio de luxo, no dia 13 de agosto. A ordem judicial foi cumprida durante a Operação Aposta Suja foi deflagrada pelo Ministério Público da Bahia (MP-BA) e pelo Ministério Público do Rio de Janeiro (MP-RJ).

No imóvel de Bruno Karttos, foram apreendidos dinheiro em espécie em moeda estrangeira, um tablet, um celular e dois veículos de alto padrão.

Todo o material será devolvido ao empresário. As contas do empresário, que foram bloqueadas durante a investigação, também serão liberadas.

Bruno Karttos, dono do time de futebol Feira Futebol Clube, foi alvo de uma operação na quinta-feira (13) — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

Natural de Feira de Santana , Bruno Karttos atua principalmente no mercado digital e de apostas esportivas. Ele é um dos fundadores da Mansão Green, empresa criada em 2023 ao lado do empresário Neto Lima.

A empresa atua no segmento de marketing e negócios digitais e reúne atividades relacionadas a influenciadores e ao mercado de iGaming, termo usado para definir a indústria de jogos e apostas pela internet. Registros empresariais consultados mostram Bruno Karttos como sócio-administrador da empresa.

Karttos também utiliza as redes sociais para falar sobre futebol e apostas. No Instagram, reúne centenas de milhares de seguidores e publica conteúdos ligados ao esporte e ao mercado de apostas.

Ele e Neto Lima também aparecem à frente do Grupo Royalty, que reúne outras empresas e negócios ligados aos dois empresários.

Neto Lima (esquerda) e Bruno Karttos posam com o mascote do Feira FC — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

A ligação de Bruno Karttos com o futebol ganhou uma nova dimensão em 2026, com a criação do Feira Futebol Clube.

O clube foi fundado para disputar a Segunda Divisão do Campeonato Baiano e surgiu como uma Sociedade Anônima de Futebol (SAF). O projeto foi idealizado pelo empresário e advogado Marcus Rios e contou com a participação de Neto Lima e Bruno Karttos. Os dois foram apresentados pelo clube como embaixadores e investidores do projeto.

O Feira FC chamou atenção ainda antes de estrear oficialmente por apostar em nomes conhecidos do futebol e das redes sociais. Entre os contratados esteve o atacante Thiago Galhardo, ex-jogador da Seleção Brasileira, além do goleiro Sidão e do influenciador Lucaneta.

A equipe terminou a primeira fase da Segunda Divisão do Campeonato Baiano na quarta colocação e avançou para o playoff do acesso. O time, no entanto, foi eliminado pelo Fluminense de Feira e não conseguiu chegar à elite do futebol baiano.

A ligação entre futebol e o mercado de apostas também aparece na própria trajetória empresarial de Karttos. A Mansão Green, empresa da qual ele é um dos fundadores, esteve ligada ao patrocínio do Campeonato Baiano de 2026.

No imóvel de Bruno Karttos, foram apreendidos dinheiro em espécie em moeda estrangeira, um tablet, um celular e veículos de alto padrão. — Foto: MP-BA

A atuação empresarial de Bruno Karttos passou a ser analisada pelas autoridades no contexto da Operação Aposta Suja.

Segundo o Ministério Público, o grupo investigado seria responsável por operar sites de apostas sem autorização do Ministério da Fazenda. De acordo com as apurações, os valores depositados pelos usuários seriam direcionados para empresas de fachada.

As investigações apontam ainda que clientes teriam sido impedidos de sacar valores disponíveis nas plataformas.

O dinheiro obtido com o esquema, segundo o MP, teria passado por diferentes operações financeiras. Parte dos recursos teria sido convertida em criptoativos, distribuída entre diversas contas e enviada para o exterior.

Um Relatório de Inteligência Financeira (RIF) do Conselho de Controle de Atividades Financeiras (Coaf) identificou mais de 800 comunicações de operações consideradas suspeitas envolvendo os investigados entre 2022 e 2026.

As movimentações identificadas ultrapassaram R$ 1,4 bilhão. Segundo o Ministério Público, mais de R$ 100 milhões foram movimentados por apenas uma das empresas investigadas.

Ao todo, foram cumpridos sete mandados de busca e apreensão na Bahia, no Rio de Janeiro e em São Paulo.

Defesa diz que ainda não teve acesso aos autos

A defesa de Bruno Karttos informou que não faria um pronunciamento oficial neste momento porque ainda não teve acesso aos autos do processo. Segundo os advogados, uma manifestação será apresentada assim que a defesa analisar o conteúdo da investigação.

O Feira Futebol Clube também se manifestou e afirmou ter "total confiança" na inocência de Karttos. O clube disse ainda que respeita a atuação das autoridades e o devido processo legal.

A investigação está em andamento, e Bruno Karttos não foi condenado pelos crimes investigados.

articles.title: Bordalás: “Pido respeto para el Getafe, si presumimos de profesionales tenemos que serlo con todos”
articles.standfirst: El técnico azulón, muy crítico con las decisiones arbitrales en las tres primeras jornadas de LaLiga
articles.summary: El técnico azulón, muy crítico con las decisiones arbitrales en las tres primeras jornadas de LaLiga
articles.body: El Getafe caía este lunes en el cierre de la tercera jornada de LaLiga. El gol de penalti de Budimir dejaba los tres puntos en El Sadar y José Bordalás analizaba el duelo que, para el entrenador getafense, no reflejó lo que de verdad mereció el equipo. Además, señaló que el penalti sobre Budimir llega tras una falta sobre Djené: “Pido respeto”, señaló el entrenador. Partido: “Estamos dolidos, creo que no hemos merecido la derrota, hemos sido mucho mejores, pero los detalles marcan los partidos. Llevamos tres encuentros que nos han penalizado con una expulsión y dos penaltis muy rigurosos”. Lesionados: “El único que puede tener algo es Andrés García, espero que no sea nada importante. El resto, la fatiga normal, han jugado los mismos, a ver si en las últimas horas llegan los refuerzos”. Penalti: “Sí, hay una falta clara a Djené, se obvia y estamos, no acostumbrados, pero... juzguen ustedes, no nos sorprende. Luego cuando hablo se molestan, pero no nos tratan de la misma manera. Cuando hay que sacar nos cuentan claramente y con ellos el portero se ha ido a celebrar una jugada absurda claramente. Es lo que hay, juzguen ustedes, toca seguir, pero vamos a seguir peleando a muerte, somos un equipo que no va a bajar los brazos. Por favor, pido respeto, vamos a seguir trabajando con la misma humildad. Si presumimos de profesionales, tenemos que serlo con todos”. Bajar los brazos: “Al final ellos se han encontrado con el penalti y se han dedicado a defender en bloque bajo, el equipo ha tenido momentos de lucidez, se ha anulado el empate, no lo he podido ver, pero me dicen que prácticamente no había nada de distancia. Tenemos que convivir con ello”. Récord de titularidades de David Soria: “Conseguirlo demuestra el nivel de compromiso, la profesionalidad y nos alegramos sobre todo por él, va a ser un récord difícil de superar, es un grandísimo profesional, un chaval magnífico y un magnífico compañero”.

articles.title: Amid expulsion talk, Lane Kiffin says LSU intends to comply with SEC orders regarding NFL players: 'Of course we will'
articles.summary: Instead of focusing on Saturday's Clemson matchup, Kiffin spent Monday largely addressing the firestorm engulfing his LSU program before he's coached a singl...
articles.body:
With potential expulsion from the SEC on the table , LSU football coach Lane Kiffin said Monday his program has no intention of defying conference rules regarding former NFL players on its football roster.

The first-year LSU head coach addressed the firestorm during his first game-week news conference with the program ahead of Saturday's season debut against Clemson.

There was little talk of Clemson on Monday, and the first question Kiffin faced regarded whether players who had signed NFL contracts would make LSU's final roster, which faces a Friday deadline to be settled. Doing so would be in violation of SEC rules established last week prohibiting teams in any sport from rostering players who had signed professional contracts.

Kiffin said that he has no intention of defying any SEC rules, which are being contested pending a court hearing on Thursday.

"So we'll wait till this week to see if there's any more guidance," Kiffin said, regarding that court hearing. "And the question whether myself as the head coach of football and will football follow SEC orders? … Of course, we will."

Multiple players from NFL training camps are on LSU's preseason roster

Kiffin faced the line of questioning days head of the SEC's deadline to set rosters for the season at 105 players. Tight end Dae'Quan Wright and defensive tackle Zxavian Harris, who played for Kiffin at Ole Miss, have reportedly signed with the program and practiced ahead of Saturday's Clemson game.

Wright signed a contract with the Philadelphia Eagles before joining the Cleveland Browns for their training camp. He was waived by the Browns. Harris signed with the New Orleans Saints and was also waived.

Edge rusher Jack Pyburn, who spent training camp with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, also joined LSU in the preseason, but was reportedly claimed on waivers by the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday and will return to the NFL.

Local judge greenlit eligibility in defiance of NCAA

All of them joined LSU after a court ruling by Baton Rouge-based District Court Judge William Jorden granted more than 40 former NCAA athletes from the 2022 recruiting class a fifth year of eligibility in conflict with an NCAA ruling restricting them. The NCAA recently passed its "five in five" model granting athletes five years of eligibility, but it did not apply to the 2022 class.

Jorden's ruling led to a wave of players who had signed pro contracts attempting to return to college on NIL deals, several with LSU.

The SEC, Big Ten, Big 12 and ACC responded with their own resolutions barring players who had been drafted by pro teams or signed pro contracts from playing for their programs. That same Baton Rouge judge on Friday accepted an amended temporary restraining order that restored those athletes' eligibility and prohibited the SEC's planned effort to punish schools in defiance of its rule.

SEC in compliance, but considering drastic measures

The SEC on Saturday communicated its intent to comply with the restraining order. But sources told Yahoo Sports' Ross Dellenger that the SEC is exploring its options to address LSU's plans to add former pros to its rosters with consequences on the table including member teams boycotting competition against LSU and even expulsion from the conference.

The next step for all parties hinges on another hearing in a Baton Rouge court scheduled for Thursday in which a judge will determine if the temporary restraining order striking down the SEC's ban of pro players will be more permanent until a trial is held. That's two days before LSU-Clemson.

Thursday hearing looms over LSU's season opener Saturday

Which brings us to Kiffin's news conference on Monday with his program at the center of a firestorm before he's coached a single game at LSU. Kiffin told reporters that his program was awaiting that Thursday decision before deciding how to move forward.

"There's no intent nor there ever was to play somebody that we're not supposed to over an SEC rule," Kiffin said. "I'm not the spokesperson. I think now you're waiting to see Thursday.

"The SEC had a stance, made a rule. The judge felt that they couldn't do that to the players. We'll be practicing, focused on Clemson and spending our time on that all week. They can figure out the rest, and we'll just wait for guidance."

Kiffin said that Wright had been practicing with the program. He contends that the player has done so in compliance with the SEC and that the conference's rules as they stand only prohibit players from being on the roster after final cuts on Friday. He made no mention of Harris when asked about who was practicing with the team.

"I can tell you that Dae'Quan practiced," Kiffin said. "And the SEC knows that. We asked them before.

"Again, that's in no violation of any previous rule or even the rule that's out there now. The new rule does not prohibit that. It strictly talks about that final roster when you make your 105 Friday."

Kiffin reiterated that LSU intends to comply with "what the SEC guides us to do" specifically regarding players like Wright.

Kiffin was also asked Monday if the chaos this has created is worthwhile. He said that he's comfortable with chaos and that he took the decision of bringing these players on board to the leaders on his roster. Per Kiffin, 'every one' of them was on board.

"I've lived in chaos for a long time. I like to say chaos is OK as long as it's controlled chaos, especially in this room with your players. … I've said it before to our staff, to our players. We're gonna have chaos. But we're gonna have controlled chaos. And our team is gonna understand why we do what we do. Just like in this decision about potentially taking players.

"I went to the players, 'What do you want to do?' And they wanted to do it. It's not like it's chaos that comes in and they don't understand it. Which is the only thing that matters. It doesn't matter if national media understands why we do what we do for our team, or other fan bases. It just matters that these guys do."

articles.title: Harvey Elliott aterriza en Valencia: "Espero llevar a este gran club a competición europea"
articles.standfirst: El mediapunta zurdo llega procedente del Liverpool cedido sin opción de compra
articles.summary: El mediapunta zurdo llega procedente del Liverpool cedido sin opción de compra
articles.body: Harvey Elliott ya está en Valencia para convertirse en nuevo jugador del club blanquinegro. El futbolista inglés aterrizó este lunes en el aeropuerto de Manises para completar los últimos trámites de su incorporación al conjunto de Mestalla, a la espera de superar el reconocimiento médico y firmar el contrato que le vinculará al club blanquinegro hasta el final de la presente temporada. “Espero poder llevar al Valencia a jugar competición europea”, dijo el futbolista inglés preguntado por sus retos personales. “El Valencia es un club increíble y quiero hacer todo lo posible por ellos. Creo que, especialmente con el equipo que tenemos, somos capaces de conseguirlo. Va a ser una temporada difícil, pero tengo mucha confianza”, añadió. La llegada del internacional inglés sub-21 supone uno de los movimientos más destacados del Valencia en el tramo final del mercado. El acuerdo con el Liverpool contempla una cesión hasta junio de 2027 sin opción de compra, una fórmula que ha permitido desbloquear una operación que parecía compleja por las condiciones económicas del futbolista. Además, ambas entidades han alcanzado un entendimiento para repartir el coste salarial durante la duración del préstamo: “Para ser sincero, todo sucedió bastante rápido, pero estaba preparado para recibir la llamada. Solo tenía que asegurarme de estar listo para venir aquí y jugar, y lo estoy. Ahora estoy aquí y tengo muchas ganas de que llegue el fin de semana”, explicó el jugador del Liverpool. Elliott, de 23 años, llega a Mestalla después de varios días de contactos entre todas las partes. La dirección deportiva valencianista aceleró las negociaciones durante las últimas jornadas y encontró en el jugador una predisposición total para recalar en LaLiga. También resultó importante la intervención del técnico Carlos Corberán, que trasladó personalmente al futbolista el papel que podría desempeñar dentro del proyecto deportivo. “Es un club increíble y estoy muy agradecido por la oportunidad. Voy a dar lo mejor de mí aquí y sé la historia que tiene este club. Todo esto requiere mucho trabajo y, por mi parte, voy a darlo todo por el Valencia”, expresaba Elliott. Formado en las categorías inferiores del Fulham y fichado por el Liverpool en 2019, Elliott está considerado como uno de los talentos más destacados de su generación en Inglaterra. A lo largo de su trayectoria ha actuado como mediapunta, interior y extremo derecho, destacando por su calidad técnica, visión de juego y capacidad para generar ventajas en los últimos metros: “Puedo jugar en cualquier posición. Simplemente estoy feliz de jugar al fútbol, pero creo que como mediapunta, como número 10, es donde soy más efectivo”, precisó la nueva incorporación del Valencia.

articles.title: Herrando sufre una lesión en el aductor y Aimar Oroz, en el bíceps femoral
articles.standfirst: Ambos futbolistas deberán ser sometidos a pruebas esta semana en la Clínica Universidad de Navarra
articles.summary: Ambos futbolistas deberán ser sometidos a pruebas esta semana en la Clínica Universidad de Navarra
articles.body: Jorge Herrando tuvo que abandonar el encuentro ante el Getafe en el minuto 39 tras una pugna con Enes Ünal en la que se hizo daño. El defensa, muy dolorido, se marchó del campo en camilla. Tras unas primeras exploraciones y según el parte médico de Osasuna, Herrando sufre una lesión en el aductor de su pierna izquierda y será sometido a pruebas en los próximos días para valorar el alcance exacto de la lesión. No fue el único rojillo que acabó con problemas el encuentro ante el Getafe. Aimar Oroz, por su parte, sufre una lesión en el bíceps femoral de su pierna izquierda y también tendrá que ser sometido a pruebas en la Clínica Universidad de Navarra para valorar el alcance exacto. Ambos futbolistas quedan pendientes de evolución.

articles.title: Everton reportedly acquiring USMNT star Folarin Balogun from Monaco in $52.3 million transfer
articles.summary: Balogun has reportedly agreed to a four-year deal with a one-year option as part of the transfer back to England.
articles.body:
Folarin Balogun is on the move. After three seasons with Ligue 1 side Monaco, the star United States men's national team forward is reportedly heading to Everton as part of a massive transfer, per soccer insider Fabrizio Romano .

Multiple reports indicated Monday that Monaco and Everton had agreed to a deal around €45 million ($52.3 million USD), plus around €5 million ($5.8 million) in potential add-ons.

Per Romano, Balogun has agreed to a four-year deal with a one-year option. He is cleared to travel and will undergo a physical before the deal is complete.

The move comes just before the Premier League's summer transfer window closes on Tuesday, with Everton hoping to start the season with an enhanced attack. In a seemingly related move, Everton also agreed to bring back Manchester City's Jack Grealish for another season on loan, per multiple reports .

Balogun was excellent for Monaco last year, scoring 13 goals and adding four assists across the season. The striker notched nine goals in Monaco's final 12 games of the regular season, though the French heavyweight finished the year in seventh. Balogun ended the year fourth in Ligue 1's individual scoring table.

Balogun's club showing was buoyed by a breakout showing in the USMNT's World Cup run this summer. Though marred by the red card controversy surrounding his final appearance in the knockout stage , Balogun finished the tournament with three goals on the way to the U.S.'s largest World Cup win and its first knockout stage win in more than two decades.

The move will mark a return to England for Balogun, who was raised in London, grew up in Arsenal's academy and started his career with the Gunners before heading to France in 2023. (The 25-year-old forward's U.S. eligibility stems from his birth in New York City after his mother was barred from returning to England due to being too far along in her pregnancy.)

Balogun becomes the latest USMNT player to earn a splashy transfer after breaking out at the 2026 World Cup. Midfielder Sebastian Berhalter, who played in all five World Cup matches after becoming an unlikely mainstay of the U.S. team, was transferred from the Vancouver Whitecaps to Championship League side Middlesbrough in July. Defender Max Arfsten joined him a week later .

articles.title: Liverpool finally get their man: $144M Bradley Barcola becomes second-most expensive signing
articles.summary: Football News: Liverpool have completed the signing of Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain, with the 23-year-old forward joining the Reds on a long-term contrac.
articles.body: Liverpool have completed the signing of Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain, with the 23-year-old forward joining the Reds on a long-term contract after passing his medical and completing the formalities of the transfer.The deal is worth a guaranteed £106 million ($144m), according to ESPN sources, with a further £17m ($23m) available in performance-related add-ons. That makes Barcola the second-most-expensive signing in Liverpool's history, behind only Alexander Isak, who joined the club from Newcastle United for £125m last summer.Barcola has signed a five-year contract and will wear the No.29 shirt at Anfield.Speaking to Liverpoolfc.com after completing his move, Barcola said: "It's a great pride to be able to play for Liverpool. I'm very happy."It took a long time but I'm really happy today to be able to play for Liverpool and all I want is to be on the pitch and be able to play."I hope to achieve very big things. First of all, winning the Premier League – it's one of my biggest dreams in my life."It is to do that and to stay in this team in the long term – that's why I signed a long contract – and I hope I can do it."Why Barcola chose LiverpoolBarcola had been a long-term Liverpool target and, according to ESPN sources, was unwilling to consider alternative destinations this summer as he pushed for a move away from PSG.The France international had become an important part of PSG's recent success, making 152 appearances, scoring 39 goals and providing 35 assists during his three-year spell in Paris. He won back-to-back Champions League titles and three successive Ligue 1 crowns with the club.His departure comes after competition for places at PSG prompted him to look for a new opportunity, with Liverpool offering him the chance to take on a major role in their attack.Barcola had also previously played twice at Anfield and said those experiences helped convince him that Liverpool was the right destination."I had the chance to play twice in this stadium and I saw the atmosphere and how the fans were behind the Liverpool players."When I knew about Liverpool's interest in me, I didn't ask questions and I knew it was a very big club for me."Barcola's career before LiverpoolBarcola began his senior career with Lyon, making his first-team debut in November 2021. He went on to make 47 appearances for the French club, scoring seven goals and providing 11 assists before joining PSG in August 2023.He made 49 appearances for PSG last season, scoring 13 goals and registering seven assists.The forward has also established himself as a France international since making his debut in June 2024. He has won 28 caps and scored six goals, including three during this summer's World Cup, where he featured in every match as France finished fourth.At Liverpool, he becomes the club's third permanent signing of the summer after Víctor Muñoz and Jérémy Jacquet, while Ronald Araújo has also arrived from Barcelona on a season-long loan.Barcola's arrival also comes with uncertainty around Cody Gakpo, with Manchester City having made an approach for the Liverpool forward. ESPN sources say Liverpool are unlikely to make another first-team signing before Tuesday's transfer deadline unless there are further departures, although Gakpo's exit would require the club to find a suitable replacement.For now, Liverpool have secured one of Europe's most sought-after young forwards, with Barcola arriving at Anfield determined to turn a long-awaited transfer into a new chapter of his career.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Other than occasional fights’: Argentina’s first Haiti-born U-17 player Kiki Ramos speaks out on racism claims
articles.summary: Football News: Kiki Ramos, the Haiti-born winger who recently became the first player born in the Caribbean country to represent Argentina, has pushed back against c.
articles.body: Kiki Ramos, the Haiti-born winger who recently became the first player born in the Caribbean country to represent Argentina, has pushed back against criticism surrounding racism and discrimination in Argentina, saying he has never personally experienced it since arriving in the country as a baby.The 17-year-old made his Argentina U-17 debut this week in a 2-1 victory over Ecuador, marking a significant moment for a player whose journey to the Albiceleste began after the devastating earthquake that struck Haiti in January 2010.Ramos was born in Haiti on April 3, 2009, and arrived in Argentina at nine months old after being adopted by an Argentine couple. He has since developed through Vélez Sarsfield and is now attracting attention from clubs in Europe.Ramos responds to criticism surrounding ArgentinaAmid criticism of Argentina and allegations of racism circulating on social media, Ramos gave his own account of his experience in the country. Speaking as quoted by Albiceleste Talk, he said:"Did I feel any racism or discrimination in Argentina? Ever since I came to Argentina, I’ve never felt discriminated against.”“Other than the occasional fights between youth players during matches, everything has always been fine off the pitch. I never felt discriminated against, and I never felt different from anyone else. That’s why I feel like people who say Argentina is racist are just saying it for the sake of it."Ramos added:"I think we’re just going through a period where Argentina is being heavily criticised, you know? But Argentina is a beautiful country. For me, it’s a dream to represent Argentina and a huge honour to wear this beautiful shirt. I’ve dreamed of it since I was a little kid, and I hope I can live up to it every time I’m called up.”Ramos' remarkable journey to the Argentina shirtRamos, who goes by "Kiki", survived the 7.0-magnitude earthquake that devastated Haiti in January 2010. The disaster caused more than 100,000 deaths, with an official figure of 316,000 later provided by Haiti's government, according to the material surrounding his story.After arriving in Argentina as a nine-month-old, Ramos was adopted by an Argentine family and eventually began his football development at Vélez Sarsfield. His emergence with the club has now taken him into Argentina's youth setup, where his debut came in the 2-1 win over Ecuador.His appearance has also attracted attention because of the historical context around players born outside Argentina representing the national team. According to the reports, Ramos could become the first player without Argentine roots to play an official match for the senior Argentina side since Paraguayan-born Heriberto Correa represented the Albiceleste after becoming an Argentine citizen in 1973.There is an unusual link between the two players beyond their birthplace circumstances: both arrived at Argentina's national-team setup while representing Vélez Sarsfield, although more than five decades separate their stories.Ramos' next major opportunity could come with Argentina's U-17 side at the 2026 FIFA U-17 World Cup, which will be held in Qatar from November 19 to December 13.For now, though, his focus is on building his career with Vélez and continuing to earn opportunities in Argentina's youth teams, while his comments offer a personal account that contrasts with the broader criticism surrounding the country and its football culture.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: GOATbye: Leo blows whistle on Messimerising international career
articles.summary: Football News: It was morning in Miami and late evening in India as Lionel Messi’s announcement through an Instagram post flooded social media. Having seen him light.
articles.body: It was morning in Miami and late evening in India as Lionel Messi’s announcement through an Instagram post flooded social media. Having seen him light up our lives for two decades, the world suddenly felt strangely empty, unfamiliar. His great rival Cristiano Ronaldo must feel so lonely today.“After all this time since the (2026 World Cup) final, and after thinking about it a lot, I want to tell everyone I’m retiring from the national team…”The post showed three handwritten pages in Spanish, in which the Argentina captain confirmed he is retiring from the Albiceleste.As a footnote, he added: “I wrote these words on July 21, two days after the final. Today, after what happened with my dad, I am even more convinced than before.”Messi’s father, Jorge Messi, died on Aug 8 at a hospital in the central Argentine city of Rosario. He was 68.“It was a decision that hurt and still hurts deep inside, but I understand that this is the right moment.”Messi is 39, and after two decades of watching him adorn the hallowed blue-and-white striped shirt, many will lament his decision to go, but no one can question it.Having lit up six World Cups, winning the tournament in Qatar 2022 and leading Argentina to the final in 2014 and 2026 — an incredible journey from wunderkind to the champion elder of the beautiful game — he held the world in a thrall.For over a decade, modern football was defined by the transcendent rivalry between Messi and the Portugal superstar Cristiano, an era-defining battle that eclipsed clubs, countries, and competitions. It was unbelievable theatre. It had to end someday.Even in a life as hallowed as his, such a difficult call needs a real breaking point. Exactly 10 years ago, after the 2016 Copa America final loss to Chile, Messi had called it a day, frustrated at the world, Argentina’s cursed fortunes and, somewhat unbelievably, in doubt about his abilities.An outpouring of concern from his team, earnest pleas from countrymen — and the rest of the world — forced a reversal.His words then were telling.“A lot of things went through my mind on the night of the final and I gave serious thought to quitting, but my love for my country and this shirt is too great. We need to fix many things in Argentinian football, but I prefer to do this from inside and not criticise from outside.”Things didn’t change immediately, though. Argentina’s World Cup debacle in Russia 2018, with Messi further cutting a lonely, isolated figure, as Luka Modric first, and then Mbappe, then only 18, tore through his team, only reinforced the sinking feeling that it was not to be.Slowly, though, it changed. New coach, old teammate Lionel Scaloni structured the team around him, gave him the freedom, appreciation and confidence he needed. All this, with a band of adoring, talented players around him.What followed was a monumental Copa America triumph — beating Neymar’s Brazil 1-0 at the famed Maracana, the same venue where he first lost a final in 2014 — marking his first major international trophy.Qatar would prove his high noon, a series of dazzling, often otherworldly performances that would earn him the World Cup winner’s medal that he so richly deserved and that had eluded him for so long. It sanctified his seat in the pantheon.This summer, in America, too, the highest-scoring man in South American football history led Argentina to the final before a young Spain proved insurmountable.Messi calls time as his country’s all-time leading goal scorer and most capped player.In 2016, Messi’s first announcement had sprung from the failures on the pitch and repeated questions on his loyalty to Argentina. But he just chipped away to finally turn things on their head. The heartbreak of the 2014 Maracana final and a string of continental disappointments had weighed heavily on him.In 2016, after blasting his penalty over the bar in the Copa America Centenario final against Chile, his call to quit international football was emotional and abrupt.“I tried so hard to be champion with Argentina. I couldn’t do it,” Messi had rued.But Argentina wasn’t ready to let him go. “No te vayas” — don’t go — became the weeping cry of a nation desperate to hold on to him.Messi gave himself a second chance.From being a prisoner of ‘dependencia’ — Argentina’s dependence on him — to the bearer of the proverbial cross, Messi’s ‘back nine’ expedition was sprinkled with trophies.Usually reticent, unwilling to pour out his heart, Messi redefined himself in his last World Cup. After scoring his first World Cup hat-trick against Algeria and launching Argentina’s title defence, Messi opened up.“Everything I’m experiencing now is a bonus. I’ve been fortunate enough to achieve all my dreams — or even more than I ever dreamed of achieving — both professionally and personally.”Two months down the line and a bereavement must have precipitated that lack of meaning and motivation. Not like the prince of Denmark, who sought revenge to restore order in a distorted world, though. More akin to calm of mind, all passion spent.Of course the universe of football will be asking for more, but Messi’s personal loss, perhaps, asked for a realignment. Argentina must learn to live with it.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Japanese Zion Suzuki makes Premier League history, but Bukayo Saka sinks Aston Villa
articles.summary: Football News: Arsenal secured a narrow 1-0 victory over Aston Villa on Monday, maintaining their perfect start to the Premier League season. Bukayo Saka’s second-ha.
articles.body: Arsenal secured a narrow 1-0 victory over Aston Villa on Monday, maintaining their perfect start to the Premier League season. Bukayo Saka’s second-half goal proved enough in a tight contest where both teams struggled to create clear chances.Villa started brightly, with Emiliano Buendia hitting the crossbar from distance, but Arsenal gradually took control and finished the first half stronger. New Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki also made history as the first Japanese goalkeeper to play in the Premier League.Arsenal thought they had won a penalty early in the second half when Saka went down after a challenge from Ian Maatsen, but a VAR review changed the decision to a free kick.Saka eventually found the breakthrough in the 59th minute. He finished from close range after good work involving Eberechi Eze and Riccardo Calafiori.Villa face tough rebuildThe result leaves Arsenal among four teams with six points from their opening two matches. Villa, meanwhile, remain without a point and have yet to register a shot on target this season.Manager Unai Emery has a major rebuilding job ahead after more than half of the players who started Villa’s Europa Cup final victory in May have left. Nicolas Jackson and Suzuki were among the new arrivals handed starts against Arsenal.Despite Villa’s energetic opening and Arsenal’s second-half pressure, neither side managed to dominate for long, with clear-cut opportunities at a premium. In the end, Saka’s goal was enough to give the defending champions another hard-earned victory.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'My daughter will be very proud': Lionel Messi's teammates pay heartfelt tribute
articles.summary: Football News: NEW DELHI: Lionel Messi’s decision to retire from international football has triggered emotional tributes from his Argentina teammates, who thanked th.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Lionel Messi’s decision to retire from international football has triggered emotional tributes from his Argentina teammates, who thanked the legendary captain for his leadership, friendship and role in their greatest successes.Goalkeeper Emi Martinez praised Messi for helping him become a world champion, while Angel Di Maria thanked him for choosing Argentina and taking the country “to the top of the world”.Rodrigo highlighted Messi’s dedication and humanity, saying, “Your unconditional love for our country, your inner battles to never give up, your strength to always endure injustice, your leadership and humanity with every player who stepped onto the training ground, making sure they felt comfortable, and the care you showed every member of staff in our national team... Just thank you. The greatest of all time. Thank you for making us so incredibly happy. You can't imagine how many smiles you brought to our faces!! You are eternal.”Lisandro’s tribute was especially personal. “My daughter will be very proud that her father shared a team with such an extraordinary human being,” he wrote, while calling Messi the “greatest athlete in history.”Lautaro Martinez also thanked Messi for the lessons he taught the squad beyond football. “Thank you for every piece of advice, every talk, every training session, every hug, and every moment shared. Thank you for making history with us and for allowing us to be a part of your story. We're going to miss you so much, captain. We'll be eternally grateful to have shared this journey with you. Thank you for everything, captain,” Martinez said.Messi closes Argentina chapterLeandro Paredes admitted he “wasn't ready” for the announcement, calling Messi a great teammate and friend.Messi announced his retirement more than a month after Argentina’s 1-0 World Cup final loss to Spain and shortly after the death of his father, Jorge Messi.“After all this time since the final, and after thinking about it a lot, I want to tell everyone that I'm retiring from the national team. It was a decision that hurt and still hurts deep inside, but I understand that this is the right moment,” Messi wrote in his retirement note.Messi leaves Argentina as its most-capped player and leading scorer, with 203 appearances and 124 goals.He won the 2021 and 2024 Copa America titles and the 2022 World Cup. He will continue playing for Inter Miami in MLS.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Liquidación del Guangzhou Evergrande, el gigante chino que fichó a estrellas y al futbolista más caro del mundo
articles.standfirst: El Guangzhou Evergrande ganó títulos y cubrió de oro a Robinho, Paulinho, Jackson Martínez, Darío Conca, Fabio Cannavaro, Luiz Felipe Scolari...
articles.summary: El Guangzhou Evergrande ganó títulos y cubrió de oro a Robinho, Paulinho, Jackson Martínez, Darío Conca, Fabio Cannavaro, Luiz Felipe Scolari...
articles.body: Un tribunal de Cantón (sureste de China) abrió formalmente el procedimiento de liquidación por quiebra del Guangzhou FC, antiguo Guangzhou Evergrande y uno de los clubes más laureados del fútbol chino, después de años de dificultades financieras vinculadas al colapso de su antiguo accionista mayoritario, el grupo inmobiliario Evergrande. El Tribunal Popular Intermedio de Cantón anunció que aceptó este lunes la solicitud de liquidación presentada por Guangzhou Zhonghang Service Management contra el equipo y designó un equipo de liquidación como administrador de la institución. Los acreedores tendrán hasta el 30 de noviembre para comunicar sus créditos y la primera junta quedó fijada para el 8 de diciembre. La decisión llega después de que el club no obtuviera a comienzos de 2025 la licencia necesaria para participar en las competiciones profesionales chinas al no haber logrado reunir fondos suficientes para saldar su deuda, circunstancia que ya entonces lo dejó al borde de la desaparición. El Guangzhou FC vivió su época de mayor éxito bajo el nombre de Guangzhou Evergrande, después de que el gigante inmobiliario homónimo adquiriera el equipo en 2010. El conjunto ganó ocho títulos de la Superliga china y conquistó dos veces la Liga de Campeones asiática, en 2013 y 2015. Por sus filas pasaron futbolistas como los brasileños Robinho y Paulinho, el colombiano Jackson Martínez y el argentino Darío Conca (que fue el futbolista mejor pagado del mundo), mientras que entre sus entrenadores figuraron Fabio Cannavaro y Luiz Felipe Scolari. Los problemas del club se agravaron en paralelo a la crisis de Evergrande, que entró en impago en 2021 tras acumular un pasivo de cientos de miles de millones de dólares. El equipo descendió de la máxima categoría en 2022 y posteriormente trató de mantenerse en la segunda división antes de quedar fuera del fútbol profesional. El caso se enmarca en las dificultades que atraviesa desde hace años el fútbol profesional chino, donde más de 30 clubes han desaparecido desde 2020 entre casos de corrupción y bancarrotas. El campeonato chino atrajo en su momento de mayor músculo económico a grandes figuras del deporte rey, como el italiano Marcello Lippi y el mencionado Scolari, ambos campeones del Mundo con sus selecciones nacionales, o estrellas como los brasileños Óscar y Hulk o el marfileño Drogba.

articles.title: Arteta, con Julián Alvarez de fondo: "Hasta este martes por la noche trataremos de mejorar el Arsenal"
articles.standfirst: Mikel Arteta analiza la posición del Arsenal antes del cierre del mercado de fichajes
articles.summary: Arteta, sobre fichajes: "Hasta este martes por la noche trataremos de mejorar el equipo"
articles.body: Mikel Arteta, entrenador del Arsenal, explicó tras el triunfo por 0-1 contra el Aston Villa, que el club londinense va "a tratar de mejorar el equipo" durante el último día del mercado de fichajes, cuyo plazo concluye este martes por la noche, sin revelar ni las posiciones ni los nombres que interesan. "Como ya he dicho, estamos tratando de mejorar el equipo y hasta este martes por la noche vamos a intentar hacerlo. He estado desconectado del mundo durante 24 horas, porque creo que mi energía probablemente tiene que estar en el partido, pero volveré a ella ahora", declaró el técnico, según recoge la página web oficial de su club. El Arsenal ha sido vinculado a un interés por el delantero del Atlético de Madrid Julián Alvarez (Atlético de Madrid), tras su frustrado fichaje por el Barcelona durante este verano. Preguntado Arteta por si necesita más recursos en su plantilla, el técnico contestó que dependerá de las lesiones que sufran durante la temporada. "Podemos hablar de ahora, pero podría cambiar. Sabíamos que si teníamos una lesión en la línea de atrás con Jurrien (Timber) fuera, estaríamos en un gran problema, así que tuvimos que fichar a Ezri (Konsa)", repasó. "Hoy, Mosquera no pudo continuar, por lo que sabemos que la profundidad de la plantilla tiene que ser realmente grande cuando estamos luchando por cuatro competiciones de la manera en que también jugamos, así que vamos a intentar hacerlo", añadió el técnico, sin revelar quién o quienes son los objetivos en el último día del mercado de fichajes.

articles.title: Lamine Yamal supera un récord de precocidad goleadora de Mbappé: más de 50 goles con 19 años y 49 días
articles.standfirst: Lamine Yamal se convirtió en el futbolista más joven de LaLiga, la Premier League, la Ligue 1, la Serie A y la Bundesliga en alcanzar los 50 goles
articles.summary: Lamine Yamal se convirtió en el futbolista más joven de LaLiga, la Premier League, la Ligue 1, la Serie A y la Bundesliga en alcanzar los 50 goles
articles.body: Con el doblete conseguido frente al Rayo Vallecano (5-2), el extremo español Lamine Yamal ya suma 51 tantos con el Barcelona, sumando todas las competiciones, y se convirtió en el jugador más joven de la historia de las cinco grandes ligas europeas en llegar al medio centenar de dianas. Así lo confirmó el club azulgrana, que destacó que, a sus 19 años y 49 días, el jugador catalán es, además, el jugador más joven de la historia de la entidad en alcanzar estos registros goleadores. Ante el Rayo, Lamine Yamal anotó el segundo tanto de su equipo, un zapatazo que entró por la escuadra, y cerró la goleada en el minuto 90 con un disparo colocado. Así, el internacional español se convirtió en el futbolista más joven de LaLiga, la Premier League, la Ligue 1, la Serie A y la Bundesliga en alcanzar los 50 tantos. De esta manera, superó a otras precoces figuras del fútbol europeo como el francés Kylian Mbappé, que llegó a los 50 goles a los 19 años y 241 días, y el noruego Erling Haaland, que lo logró cuando tenía 20 años y 196 días.

articles.title: ‘He completely changes’: Ronaldo teammate reveals what the superstar is really like behind closed doors
articles.summary: Football News: Cristiano Ronaldo has spent more than two decades being one of the most intensely scrutinised figures in football, but former teammate Álvaro González.
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo has spent more than two decades being one of the most intensely scrutinised figures in football, but former teammate Álvaro González says the personality behind the superstar image is very different once the Portuguese forward walks into the dressing room.'A true phenomenon' in the dressing roomGonzález, who shared a dressing room with Ronaldo at Al-Nassr during the 2022-23 Saudi Pro League season, was asked about his experience alongside the five-time Ballon d'Or winner during the broadcast of Racing-Elche on Radio MARCA. González joined the Saudi club in August 2022, months before Ronaldo's arrival in January 2023, and his response was emphatic: behind closed doors, Ronaldo is approachable, helpful and, despite his extraordinary competitive reputation, "a super normal" person.González said his view is not based solely on his own experience, explaining that he has also spoken to other teammates who have shared a dressing room with Ronaldo."Honestly, and after confirming it with other teammates we’ve had in common, he’s a true phenomenon in the dressing room", González said.That relaxed personality, according to the former centre-back, is quite different from what happens once Ronaldo steps onto the pitch."As soon as he goes from the dressing room to the field, he completely changes", he explained, describing Ronaldo as "a competitive beast" when it comes to playing and training.González said Ronaldo was particularly helpful when he first arrived and that the Portugal captain played an important role in helping teammates through some of the difficulties they were experiencing that year."Inside the dressing room he is a super normal, approachable person who helps you", González said."He helped us enormously when he arrived because of some things that were happening during that year, and he helped us with everything", he added.For González, seeing that side of Ronaldo firsthand made the experience of sharing a dressing room with him even more memorable."When you experience it firsthand yourself, it’s much more beautiful", he said.The former defender also reflected on the privilege of sharing a dressing room with Ronaldo and Lionel Messi, two players he believes will remain part of football history long after their careers are over."They are people, both he and Messi, who will go down in the history of sport, which is football", González said.Even the training-ground battles ended with a laughThere was also room for some lighter memories from training, particularly when González was asked whether he ever tried to get under Ronaldo's skin."Always", he replied.Any tension generated during those competitive sessions apparently did not last very long."The dirty looks... afterwards we would go to the jacuzzi, have a few laughs and some humor, and everything would pass", González said with a laugh.That competitiveness, however, was something Ronaldo wanted from those around him. González explained that the Portuguese star liked teammates to maintain a high level during training, even after moving into a different footballing environment in Saudi Arabia."He likes us to be competitive in training", González said.Ronaldo's own mentality, González suggested, was never really about slowing down. Instead, he wanted to maintain the same relentless standards and "keep going here and keep at it because we have to carry on".And there is still one enormous target driving him: reaching 1,000 career goals.Ronaldo is closing in on 1,000Ronaldo's pursuit of four figures has become one of the defining storylines of the later stage of his career, and he has continued to move closer even at 41.After scoring in Al-Nassr's 2-1 comeback victory over Al-Taawoun on August 28, Ronaldo's official senior career tally reached 978 goals, leaving him 22 short of 1,000.That latest goal was also significant for Al-Nassr itself: it made Ronaldo the club's all-time leading scorer in the Saudi Pro League era, with 104 league goals in 110 appearances.The 1,000-goal mark would be an unprecedented milestone in official senior football, and Ronaldo has made clear that it remains a major objective as he continues what could be the final stage of his playing career. Earlier this month, Ronaldo said the upcoming season could be his last, although he remains focused on continuing to play and pursuing the milestone.For González, though, the remarkable numbers and records are only one part of Ronaldo's story. Having seen him away from the cameras, he remembers a teammate who could be intensely competitive once training began, but who could just as easily laugh, help those around him and switch off with his teammates afterwards.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Joao Neves earns £150,000 a week and has won 2 Champions League titles - so why does he drive a £7,000 van?
articles.summary: Football News: João Neves has established himself as one of Paris Saint-Germain’s most important players, helping the club enjoy remarkable success in Europe while e.
articles.body: João Neves has established himself as one of Paris Saint-Germain’s most important players, helping the club enjoy remarkable success in Europe while earning a reported £150,000 a week (approx. $195,000).However, despite his status as a back-to-back Champions League winner, the Portuguese midfielder has been spotted arriving at training in a surprisingly modest vehicle: a 2021 Peugeot Partner van reportedly worth around £7,000 (approx. $9,100).A very different kind of footballer's carThe Peugeot Partner is not a new vehicle either, with the model Neves was seen driving dating back to 2021. Given his reported £150,000 weekly salary, the van is an unusually modest choice for a player operating at the very top level of European football.To put his frugality into perspective, Neves earns approximately $27,800 USD per day based on his reported weekly wage. That means he makes enough in a single day to buy roughly three of the same vans he uses to travel to training.Visuals circulating online show Neves greeting supporters outside the training ground, stopping to interact with them and signing autographs before getting back into the small white van and driving away. His friendly exchange with fans made the contrast with the usual luxury cars seen outside elite football training grounds all the more striking.The sight has also prompted plenty of surprise because footballers are often known for arriving at training in expensive cars, with luxury and performance vehicles frequently becoming almost as much of a talking point as what happens on the pitch.Neves, however, appears to have gone in the opposite direction, turning up in a practical commercial-style van that costs only a fraction of what many of his fellow professionals spend on their cars.Neves' rise at Paris Saint-GermainThe Portuguese midfielder joined PSG from Benfica in 2024 for a reported £60 million, approximately $78 million USD, and quickly established himself as an important part of Luis Enrique's side despite his age. He has since been part of a PSG team that has won back-to-back Champions League titles, while also forming a strong midfield partnership with fellow Portugal international Vitinha.Last season, Neves made 49 appearances, scoring three goals and providing 10 assists for the French champions.His understated choice of car therefore makes for an amusing contrast: one of Europe's most successful young midfielders can command a £60 million transfer fee, worth around $78 million, and a reported six-figure weekly salary, yet he is still perfectly happy arriving at training in a £7,000 ($9,100) Peugeot van.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Transfer deadline day: When does the Premier League window shut? What about Europe?
articles.summary: Transfer deadline day is upon us — and if it follows the recent trend, we can expect chaos. Clubs across Europe are frantically attempting to wrap up their s...
articles.body:
Transfer deadline day is upon us — and if it follows the recent trend, we can expect chaos.

Clubs across Europe are frantically attempting to wrap up their summer business, with a host of high-profile deals in the works.

Manchester City are looking to wrap up their move for Liverpool's Cody Gakpo , while Tottenham Hotspur are aiming to bring in Iliman Ndiaye from Everton, with Richarlison heading in the other direction.

Elsewhere across the continent, will Atletico Madrid finally negotiate with Barcelona over Julian Alvarez after their summer-long saga?

Many questions are set to be answered on Tuesday, and The Athletic will bring you all the latest through our dedicated live coverage.

When does the window close for Premier League clubs?

The transfer window officially comes to a close in England — including the Premier League, the Championship, League One and League Two — at 11pm BST on September 1.

It marks a return to the traditional late deadline, after the summer 2025 and winter 2026 deadlines were set at 7pm local time. That change was introduced to help give club staff working across transfer departments a more normal working pattern.

However, there were signs of the difficulties clubs faced in concluding their business by 7pm. Last year's summer transfer deadline day saw Liverpool's move for Marc Guehi and Leeds United's pursuit of Harry Wilson break down late in the day.

Although club staff will be required to put in some unsociable hours on Tuesday, they may welcome the extra four-hour buffer as they try to conclude their business.

However, the action may not end at 11pm — deal sheets allow clubs to conclude signings two hours after the transfer window closes, provided the correct paperwork is submitted before the deadline.

Clubs could be working in the early hours of the UK morning to get deals over the line.

All five major European leagues are set to close their transfer windows on September 1.

When English clubs adjusted their transfer window to 7pm BST, the German, French and Italian leagues followed suit (8pm local time). Spain retained its 10:59pm BST (11:59pm local time) deadline.

And despite England reverting to the 11pm cut-off, clubs in Germany, France and Italy have all retained the earlier time of 8pm (local time, 7pm BST). Spanish clubs are unchanged.

Scottish team have a further two days to conduct their business — their window closes on September 3 at 5pm.

Major League Soccer clubs are well into the 2026 campaign, and their summer transfer deadline is similarly aligned.

The "secondary transfer window" for MLS clubs got underway on July 13, later than the European windows, and it closes on September 2.

The league said it is the first time in over two decades (excluding the Covid-19-affected 2020 campaign) that a transfer window has extended into September, and that by aligning with European clubs, it has given its teams "a greater opportunity to acquire high-quality international talent".

The transfer deadline also applies to the three Canadian clubs in MLS: Montreal, Toronto and Vancouver Whitecaps.

There have been several high-profile transfers to the MLS this summer, including Robert Lewandowski joining Chicago Fire and former Manchester United midfielder Casemiro's move to Inter Miami.

Unlike in the Premier League and English Football League, Women's Super League clubs will be required to conclude transfer business before their 2026-27 season gets underway.

The WSL's transfer deadline is set at 11pm BST on Thursday, September 3.

That is just the day before the campaign gets underway, with London City Lionesses hosting Manchester United in the season opener on Friday at 7pm BST.

Like the MLS, the National Women's Soccer League (NWSL) is also well into its 2026 season, and its clubs have until September 7 to wrap up any impending business.

After this evening's deadline, there will still be some significant leagues at play in the transfer market.

Turkish clubs have provided some of the biggest talking points in the window — Mohamed Salah's move to Trabzonspor and Galatasaray's interest in Bruno Fernandes , for example.

They will be free to complete transfers until Friday, September 4. And with players in major European leagues still able to depart their clubs beyond the deadline, there is potential for big deals to still be done in the coming days.

In Saudi Arabia, the transfer window is open until October 12, according to FIFA . While it has been a less significant role for Saudi Pro League clubs this summer, several high-profile moves have still provided major talking points, with Al Hilal successful in their pursuit of Ollie Watkins , and Gabriel Martinelli also set to join.

Elsewhere, the Portuguese window is open until September 15, while in the Netherlands, business must conclude by the September 2 deadline.

articles.title: Reports: U.S. striker Folarin Balogun is headed on transfer to Premier League club Everton
articles.summary: United States striker Folarin Balogun is set to head to Premier League team Everton on a transfer from Monaco, British media reported on Monday.  The transfe...
articles.body:
LONDON (AP) — United States striker Folarin Balogun is set to head to Premier League team Everton on a transfer from Monaco, British media reported on Monday.

The transfer fee offered by Everton is reported to be in the range of 40 million pounds ($54 million) on a four-year deal, the British Press Association said. It said personal terms had yet to be worked out before the deal could be completed prior to Tuesday's transfer deadline.

The 25-year-old Balogun, who had two years remaining on a contract at Monaco, gained attention this summer scoring three goals for the United States as it reached the knockout stage of the World Cup. He was the top scorer for the U.S. team.

He also made headlines after drawing a red card and a one-game suspension in a 2-0 victory over Bosnia and Herzegovina in a round-of-32 match.

The one-game suspension was deferred by FIFA after U.S. President Donald Trump intervened, allowing Balogun to play in the round of 16. Balogun eventually played in the 4-1 loss to Belgium that ended the U.S. team's home World Cup run.

The intervention prompted a formal complaint to FIFA ethics investigators.

Balogun was born in New York but grew up in Britain. He came up through Arsenal's academy before moving to Middlesbrough, then to the French league with Reims and eventually to Monaco.

He scored 13 goals last season in 30 Ligue 1 matches.

articles.title: La selección española de fútbol financiará que sus jugadoras puedan congelar sus óvulos
articles.standfirst: La Federación Española ultima un acuerdo para facilitar a las futbolistas de la selección que congelen sus óvulos
articles.summary: La Federación Española ultima un acuerdo para facilitar a las futbolistas de la selección que congelen sus óvulos
articles.body: Europa Press confirma que la Real Federación Española de Fútbol (REFEF) última un acuerdo con una clínica de fertilidad para que las jugadoras de la selección puedan congelar óvulos y facilitar el encaje de la maternidad en su carrera deportiva. Pablo Linde avanzó en el diario 'El País' que 'la selección española de fútbol financiará la congelación de óvulos de sus jugadoras' e informó que "Alexia Putellas lo planteó a la federación y la RFEF ha respondido". "Es un avance enorme porque la Federación entiende que estás sirviendo a tu país en contra de tu tiempo biológico, que no puedes parar y no puedes ser madre porque necesitas tu cuerpo para trabajar", explicó Alexia Putellas en Sofía Ruiz de Velasco en una entrevista concedida a 'El País Semanal'. El acuerdo con la clínica de fertilidad se firmará las próximas semanas. En el tenis la WTA introdujo en junio de 2025 la denominada 'Regla de Especial Protección de la Fertilidad'. La regla significa que las jugadoras ahora pueden tomarse un tiempo fuera de la competición para someterse a un procedimiento de protección de la fertilidad, como la congelación de óvulos o embriones, y regresar a la competición de forma segura con una clasificación protegida, sin que su ranking se vea afectado por su ausencia de las pistas. Las jugadoras elegibles recibirán una Clasificación de Entrada Especial (SER), que podrá utilizarse para participar en hasta tres torneos, basándose en el promedio de 12 semanas de su Clasificación. Con esta nueva forma de protección del ranking, la WTA apoya y empodera a sus jugadoras para que puedan compaginar su carrera deportiva profesional con la planificación y la formación de una familia en el momento que elijan.

articles.title: TNT FC August Feature | The club between clubs: Why Korea’s footballers turn to TNT FC
articles.summary: Park Yong-woo is the latest Korean international to pass through TNT FC's doors, but he is certainly not the first. The Ulsan HD midfielder spent this summer...
articles.body:
Park Yong-woo is the latest Korean international to pass through TNT FC's doors, but he is certainly not the first. The Ulsan HD midfielder spent this summer training with TNT as he worked his way back to full fitness - prompting one question: just how many big names have used TNT as their training ground over the years?

Following an injury last year, Korea international midfielder Park Yong-woo joined TNT FC this summer as a training member as he prepared for his return to football. Training alongside TNT's younger players, Park worked to raise his match fitness before eventually rejoining Ulsan HD.

With TNT FC run like a professional club, it provides the ideal environment for players to keep themselves ticking over. Park isn't the only current or former international who has trained with TNT FC over the years.

TNT FC has clearly become a kind of unofficial "training/refresher home" for established Korean pros, particularly when they're between clubs, recovering from injury, or preparing to return.

The original TNT model was essentially "give players somewhere serious to train when they don't have a club." So for someone like Ki Sung-yueng, it wasn't that he was joining TNT because he needed to find a club. He was essentially using their established training environment while he was between FC Seoul contracts.

Same with Park Yong-woo: after his injury, TNT provided a proper team environment where he could train with younger players while getting his fitness and rhythm back. TNT's own announcement says he spent about a month doing exactly that before returning to K League with Ulsan.

That's a win-win situation. TNT gets elite-level experience around its younger players, while the established player gets a professional training environment.

Former national team captain Ki Sung-yueng is perhaps the biggest name to have used TNT's facilities. The midfielder trained with TNT during a period between spells with FC Seoul, making use of the club's structured environment while he was between teams.

For a player with Ki's experience, TNT was never about finding a route back into professional football. Instead, it offered something much simpler and arguably just as important: a place to train properly, with teammates, coaches and the intensity of a football environment.

Another Korea international and former national team captain, Lee Chung-yong has also trained with TNT during his career.

Like Ki, Lee was already an established professional when he joined TNT's training environment. His presence further underlines the unusual role TNT has come to play: it isn't simply a destination for players trying to make it as professionals, but somewhere even established players can turn to when they need a place to train.

Perhaps the most interesting example is Hwang Hee-chan. In an interview with The Fact, Kim Tae-ryung explained that KFA fitness coach Lee Jae-hong brought Hwang Hee-chan to TNT in late 2015. Hwang was about to leave for Austria to join Red Bull Salzburg, and rather than simply training on his own, he spent around two months training alongside TNT so they could monitor his physical condition before his departure.

And it wasn't just a favour to Hwang. He subsequently became one of TNT's supporters, with reports saying he privately provided bottled water for TNT players' training and matches.

From a young Hwang preparing for his first move to Europe to established internationals such as Ki Sung-yueng, Lee Chung-yong and Park Yong-woo, TNT has provided a place for Korean footballers at very different stages of their careers.

For TNT's players, meanwhile, the opportunity to train alongside footballers who have represented Korea and played at the highest levels of the game is an invaluable bonus.

It is a relationship that works both ways — and one that has made TNT FC much more than simply a club for players looking for their next opportunity.

articles.title: El futuro Messi: contrato en Miami hasta 2028, ¿un último Balón de Oro? y su vida fuera del fútbol
articles.standfirst: Sin la selección, Leo aún tiene objetivos... hasta que el cuerpo y la cabeza le digan 'basta'
articles.summary: Sin la selección, Leo aún tiene objetivos... hasta que el cuerpo y la cabeza le digan 'basta'
articles.body: Leo Messi sigue vigente, aunque ya no vaya a jugar con la Selección. La prueba son los cuatro goles que marcó el domingo con el Inter Miami (es el actual pichichi de la Liga con 18 dianas). O sea, futbolísticamente, hay un Leo bien vigente. No caben dudas. Otra cosa es su cabeza, sus ganas... que, seguramente, serán las que algún día digan 'basta'. Y más tras la pérdida de Jorge, su padre. Pero vayamos a los hechos concretos. Leo (LM) tiene contrato con Inter hasta finales de 2028. No obstante, y más en el caso de Leo, eso es un mero dato. Que nadie dude de que eso no significa nada. LM se retirará cuando quiera, y así lo asumirá Inter Miami, que le dará un espacio en su accionariado y en su estructura para seguir vinculado al club si él quiere. Deportivamente, a Leo le quedan algunos títulos por luchar para engordar los 48 entorchados que tiene (es el récord mundial, y sin contar los individuales). Le queda, por ejemplo, la MLS 2026, torneo en el que está inmerso ahora mismo. El Inter es el vigente campeón. Ah, y a corto plazo, nadie se atreve a descartarlo para su noveno Balón de Oro. Ojo a ese posible premio de octubre, mes en el que recibirá también el Príncipe de Asturias en Oviedo. Si su cabeza y sus piernas le dieran ganas de seguir (no hay que descartar nada ni en un sentido ni en otro), Messi tendrá también desafíos en 2027: una MLS corta hasta junio (el fútbol en Estados Unidos se reprogramará al calendario europeo el año que viene); la siguiente MLS 27-28; la ConcaChampions 2028 (un título muy querido en Miami e inédito en el club)... En fin, objetivos hay, si Leo quiere seguir. Y luego está su vida fuera del fútbol (Messi cumplirá 40 años el 24 de junio de 2027). O sea, una larga vida por delante con su familia y sus negocios, que son muchos y variados: es imagen de muchas marcas, propietario de un vino, unas bebidas energéticas... Es decir, la imagen de Leo podría dar para varias vidas, pero su familia y su entorno siempre tuvieron la inquietud de prorrogar su legado más allá del balón. El ejemplo más concreto es la compra del Unió Esportiva Cornellà, un club de la Tercera Federación de Cataluña que Leo adquirió este año como forma de perpetuar su apellido en el fútbol. Un 'juguete' pequeñito que quiere hacer grande a través de su gestión y la de su equipo en los próximos años. No en vano, recordemos que LM vivirá con mucha probabilidad en Cataluña (sigue manteniendo la casa de Castelldefels) cuando se retire del fútbol. Desde ahí, seguramente, disfrutará de la familia, gestionará sus negocios y perpetuará su legado en el fútbol desde este otro prisma, más allá de todo lo que seguramente supondrá como eterno embajador del fútbol argentino. Larga vida al 'otro' Leo.

articles.title: Otra cesión ‘salvadora’ de la Juve
articles.standfirst: Jonathan David se une a Nico Gonzalez y Tiago Mendes en el viaje Turín-Madrid
articles.summary: Jonathan David se une a Nico Gonzalez y Tiago Mendes en el viaje Turín-Madrid
articles.body: El 1 de septiembre de 2025, hace justo un año, el Atlético encontró en la Juve un aliado para cerrar el mercado. Los rojiblancos cerraron ese día la llegada de Nico González en forma de cesión. El argentino completaba la plantilla y cayó de pie, debutando a los pocos días con un gol ante el Villarreal. Este año la historia se repite con la llegada de Jonathan David a la disciplina colchonera. El delantero canadiense completa la delantera de los de Simeone y se une al Atlético, también cedido desde Turín. Pese a que el argentino se ganó un hueco entre el cuerpo técnico, su elevada opción de compra impidió su continuidad. Los rojiblancos siguieron teniendo su nombre en mente durante todo el verano, pero, tal y como adelantó MARCA, su llegada se vio truncada por la negativa de la Juve a dejarlo salir. No será el argentino quien llegue cedido; en esta ocasión será el canadiense Jonathan David quien aterrice con la intención de volver a encontrar su mejor versión. Las cesiones de Nico y Jonathan David no son las únicas operaciones entre Atlético y Juventus en forma de préstamo. Ambos equipos han vivido situaciones similares en los mercados de fichajes, con viajes de ida y vuelta. Uno de los grandes nombres de la era Simeone comenzó su andadura como rojiblanco mediante una cesión en el mercado invernal, de Turín a Madrid. Tiago Mendes vivió dos cesiones antes de convertirse definitivamente en futbolista del Atlético. El portugués firmó como rojiblanco en 2011 tras haber llegado primero cedido en enero y, posteriormente, en junio de 2010. El delantero italiano Moise Kean llegó incluso a presenciar un partido en el Metropolitano antes de incorporarse en el mercado invernal de la temporada 2024-25. Sin embargo, unos problemas en el reconocimiento médico dejaron su fichaje en el limbo. Otros nombres ilustres que hicieron el viaje de Turín a Madrid fueron Vieri y Mandzukic. Ambos llegaron traspasados y ambos solo jugaron una temporada como rojiblancos. Uno de los movimientos más recordados entre ambos equipos fue la cesión de Álvaro Morata a la Juventus. El delantero madrileño regresó al conjunto italiano directamente desde el Metropolitano. La Juventus pagó cerca de 10 millones de euros por cada temporada de cesión, pero no terminó ejecutando la opción de compra y el jugador regresó al Atlético. Un movimiento en sentido contrario al que protagonizará Jonathan David en esta ocasión.

articles.title: Al Barça le espera un cierre de mercado frenético
articles.standfirst: Casadó, Balde, el fichaje de un central, la inscripción de Livakovic...
articles.summary: Casadó, Balde, el fichaje de un central, la inscripción de Livakovic...
articles.body: Este martes, a las doce de la noche, se cierra el mercado de fichajes. El Barcelona llega a esta última jornada con algunos deberes muy importantes por cerrar. Hacía tiempo que el club azulgrana no afrontaba un cierre con tanta incertidumbre y, además, con operaciones importantes por resolver: Gabriel Jesús, Balde, Casadó, el fichaje de un central... El primer paso es el más evidente. Gabriel Jesús será anunciado oficialmente hoy como nuevo jugador del Barcelona. Aquí no hay secretos. El club azulgrana y el Arsenal llegaron el pasado fin de semana a un acuerdo para el traspaso del delantero por diez millones de euros más cuatro en variables. El brasileño ya llegó este lunes a la Ciudad Condal para pasar la revisión médica. La Dirección Deportiva tiene que resolver el futuro de Marc Casadó. Esto ya se sabía desde el final de la temporada anterior, pero las dudas del jugador han provocado que la operación no se haya solucionado hasta el último día. Tiene varias propuestas sobre la mesa. Una de ellas, la más lucrativa para el Barcelona, procede de Arabia, pero el centrocampista no acaba de ver claro ir a jugar a ese país. La vía más probable es la de Turquía. El Besiktas y otro club han mostrado interés por Casadó, que sigue dándole vueltas a esta propuesta. También hay ofertas del fútbol inglés, pero económicamente no son las mejores. Jorge Mendes ya ha presentado todas estas propuestas tanto al club como al jugador y ha llegado la hora de tomar una decisión final. El precio del traspaso rondará los 25 millones de euros. Jorge Mendes también juega un papel muy importante en el futuro de Balde. A pesar de todo lo que se ha dicho, el lateral quiere abandonar el Barcelona porque es plenamente consciente de que, por delante de él, están en este momento Cancelo y Xavi Espart. Sabe que va a jugar muy poco. Por este motivo, Mendes se ha pasado la última semana buscándole un equipo. El Manchester United estaba interesado en el jugador, pero pretende una cesión. El club azulgrana quiere una venta, pero ha tasado al defensa en 40 millones de euros y, de momento, no aparece ningún comprador. Habrá que esperar para ver qué solución encuentran para su salida. Aunque es improbable, al final el defensa podría quedarse. Y, por otra parte, quedan las incorporaciones. La de Julián Álvarez parece totalmente descartada después del fichaje de Gabriel Jesús. El Atlético sigue en sus trece y la puerta para este mercado parece totalmente cerrada. Sin embargo, lo que sí puede llegar es un central. Deco sigue buscando uno después de las salidas de Araujo y Álvaro Cortés. La salida de Balde implicaría el fichaje seguro de un defensa; si no se va, Deco tendrá que hacer números para ver cómo queda el 'Fair Play'. Y de este tema depende también la inscripción de Livakovic. El portero está a la espera de que haya hueco en la masa salarial para formar parte del primer equipo. Si no fuera así, saldría cedido a otro club. El Barcelona también debe cerrar las salidas de dos jugadores del filial que disputaron algún partido con el primer equipo la temporada pasada. Álvaro Cortés se va al Amberes y Toni Fernández, al Venezia.

articles.title: Bellingham vuelve al lugar del crimen
articles.standfirst: Liberado por Mourinho, el inglés ha recuperado su rol de llegador al área y ya suma dos goles y dos asistencias, con la estela de Lampard como espejo
articles.summary: Liberado por Mourinho, el inglés ha recuperado su rol de llegador al área y ya suma dos goles y dos asistencias, con la estela de Lampard como espejo
articles.body: Jude Bellingham ha irrumpido en la 2026/27 como un titán, y lo ha hecho regresando a la escena de sus mejores fechorías: el área rival. Su Mundial, con siete goles y una asistencia, ya anticipaba que con Mourinho tenía todas las papeletas para reencontrarse con su mejor posición. Era casi inevitable que el portugués acabara concediéndole la libertad con la que lo estamos viendo renacer, esa que nos devuelve, a estas alturas de 2026, al Bellingham deslumbrante de 2023. Y es que, en su caso, volver a la casilla de salida es una bendición. En las tres primeras jornadas de su temporada inaugural de blanco sumó cuatro goles y una asistencia jugando prácticamente de delantero. El área era entonces su coto de caza, y ahora vuelve a serlo tras dos campañas lejos de su nivel. Ya acumula dos tantos y dos asistencias en tres partidos ligueros, y todo con el añadido de que su pretemporada se limitó a 29 minutos en el amistoso ante el Schalke. Ni el óxido de las vacaciones ha podido con su instinto. Así como Ancelotti lo tuvo claro en su día, Mourinho detectó de inmediato el desaprovechamiento de Jude la temporada pasada. "He pactado con él que no quería ver a Jude defender casi como un segundo lateral izquierdo, algo que le he visto hacer muchas veces", reveló el técnico tras la victoria ante el Málaga. Una de sus mejores decisiones hasta ahora: liberar al inglés de las cadenas que lo alejaban del gol. Por primera vez en dos temporadas emerge una figura capaz de disputarle el protagonismo a Mbappé. Con regularidad resulta complicado, cierto, porque es el galo quien suele acaparar los goles y, con ellos, los focos. Es precisamente Mbappé quien se está beneficiando de que Jude vuelva a ser ese peligro desatado que pone en guardia a las defensas. Con el inglés merodeando el área, Kylian encuentra menos vigilancia, un espacio que la pasada campaña no existía porque Bellingham apenas se aproximaba a la zona de castigo. El fenómeno, en realidad, no es nuevo para los planes de Mourinho. A lo largo de su carrera, el luso ha hecho del centrocampista de segunda línea una de sus armas más temidas. El primer ejemplo lo firmó en el Oporto con Deco, aunque el brasileño respondía a un perfil más asociativo, más de dar que de rematar, y bajo su tutela se consagró como mejor jugador de la Champions que los dragones ganaron en 2004, donde repartió 10 asistencias de sus 29 totales en el curso. Después llegaron otros perfiles más incisivos. Wesley Sneijder renació a sus órdenes en el Inter del triplete de 2010, mejorando notoriamente las cifras de su etapa gris en el Madrid hasta el punto de que algunos lo reclamaron para el Balón de Oro de aquel año. Pero el gran espejo en el que Bellingham debe mirarse es Frank Lampard, su compatriota. En el Chelsea, Mourinho lo encumbró hasta convertirlo en el máximo goleador histórico del club, con 211 tantos. A las órdenes del luso firmó cerca de 71 goles, con una temporada de cifras de escándalo en la que alcanzó los 21 tantos y 21 asistencias. Ese es el techo de lo que un mediapunta puede alcanzar en sus manos, y el listón que Jude tiene ahora enfrente. Ellos marcan el camino de lo que un mediapunta puede llegar a ser en manos de Mourinho, y el inglés reúne argumentos de sobra para inscribir su nombre en esa estirpe. Si el arranque es un anticipo, el Madrid ha recuperado a su llegador más determinante justo cuando el técnico que mejor sabe explotarlo se ha sentado en su banquillo. La casilla de salida, para Bellingham, huele de nuevo a gol.
