articles.title: Lo nunca visto en la carrera de Gayà
articles.standfirst: El capitán del Valencia se queda en el banquillo en dos partidos completos seguidos por primera vez desde su debut con el primer equipo en 2014
articles.summary: El capitán del Valencia se queda en el banquillo en dos partidos completos seguidos por primera vez desde 2013
articles.body: José Luis Gayà atraviesa un momento difíccil en su carrera al que añadió un capítulo inédito a una trayectoria que parecía haber vivido todo tipo de situaciones en el Valencia. El capitán valencianista se quedó en el banquillo, sin disputar un solo minuto, en dos partidos consecutivos de Liga por primera vez desde que debutó con el primer equipo en la competición en 2014. Tras ser titular contra el Celta, el lateral izquierdo permaneció en el banquillo durante todo el encuentro ante el Betis en Mestalla y volvió a hacerlo este domingo en Riazor frente al Deportivo. No había lesión ni contratiempo físico que justificara su ausencia. Fue una decisión técnica de Carlos Corberán, que actualmente considera que Jesús Vázquez atraviesa un mejor momento para ocupar el lateral izquierdo. Desde su debut en la élite, Gayà había atravesado épocas de bonanza y de crisis, cambios de entrenador, competiciones europeas, rotaciones por la Copa, lesiones y oportunos debates sobre su rendimiento deportivo y su continuidad. Sin embargo, nunca había enlazado dos partidos ligueros seguidos viendo el encuentro completo desde el banquillo estando disponible para jugar. Gayá suma 344 partidos de Liga con el Valencia, 324 de ellos como titular. En el banquillo (partidos completos como suplente) solo ha estado en 13 ocasiones, dos de ellas en los dos últimos partidos seguidos del equipo. La situación coincide además con un momento delicado en el plano contractual. Gayà tiene vinculación con el Valencia hasta 2027, pero sobre la mesa hubo una propuesta de renovación con condiciones económicas muy inferiores, que los agentes del jugador ni tomaron en consideración. Al respecto de esta negociación y del futuro del futbolista, fue preguntado Corberán la semana pasada por si se imaginaba un Valencia sin Gayá. La respuesta fue tibia: "A día de hoy, Gayà está en el Valencia. Entonces yo me imagino un Valencia con Gayà y mi posición con respecto a él o cualquier jugador es sacar, junto a ellos, su máximo rendimiento. Y ese es mi objetivo con Gayà y con cualquier jugador”. A sus 31 años, Gayà no solo es el capitán del Valencia, sino también uno de los jugadores que representan la identidad del club blanquinegro durante más de una década. Convertido en titular indiscutible con una larga lista de entrenadores –desde Nuno en 2014-, parecía ocupar una demarcación blindada independientemente de la competencia (Siqueira y Lato, en los primeros años; más recientemente Jaume Costa o Jesús Vázquez, ahora). Es obvio que nadie dura eternamente y menos en el deporte de alto rendimiento. Pero hay situaciones deportivas que un club debe saber manejar por el simbolismo de algunos futbolistas. Con la competencia de Vázquez, a Gayá le queda intentar convencer al entrenador de que está en condiciones de pelear la titularidad aunque ya ha vivido una situación que nunca había experimentado en las 13 temporadas que lleva en la dinámica del primer equipo: dos partidos en el banquillo sin jugar.

articles.standfirst: 'Al otro lado del espejo', una opinión de Alfredo Relaño
articles.summary: 'Al otro lado del espejo', una opinión de Alfredo Relaño
articles.body: La buena cara actual del Madrid tiene varias causas, quizá la más destacable el renacimiento de Bellingham, que ha recuperado protagonismo y gol. Mbappé también ha levantado respecto al curso pasado, pero en su caso arrastró una lesión (con el descalzaperros de la rodilla equivocada) y su relación con Arbeloa llegó a ser demasiado mala. Pero sabíamos Mbappé seguía ahí, mientras que lo mejor de Bellingham empezaba a quedar muy lejos. En el Mundial ya le vimos bien, lo mismo que a Mbappé, lo que en ambos casos despertó la sospecha maliciosa de si no se habrían reservado voluntariamente para él, pero echemos pelillos a la mar. Ahora están bien, no hay Mundial en el horizonte y ambos participan, como todo el grupo, de una especie de “espíritu de enmienda” muy positivo. Yo creo que hasta se le nota a Mourinho, ajeno a estas dos últimas temporadas malas, pero consciente quizá de que algunas conductas de su primer paso por aquí no fueron buenas para nada ni para nadie. De sabios es rectificar. Volviendo a Bellingham, está jugando en su posición favorita, detrás del punta y cerca del gol, con el que emparenta con facilidad. Mourinho diseñó en torno a él un 4-2-3-1 que la práctica convierte en ocasiones en un 4-2-4, táctica común en los años sesenta, cuando conocí el fútbol y nos referíamos al centro del campo como ‘la zona ancha’, por tan pocos jugadores como se afanaban en ella, transitando de ida y vuelta. No era tanto zona de puna y elaboración como ahora, sino más bien de paso. De los cuatro de arriba, dos eran extremos, uno delantero centro en punta y el otro, un interior que se retrasaba para dar luz al ataque y llegar al remate por sorpresa. Así pueden jugar Bellingham y el Madrid partidos de trámite fácil, pero cuando salgan las corridas en puntas habrá que poblar más el medio campo. Ya veremos si sacrificando uno de los extremos y confiando ese puesto a un Güler o un Bernardo Silva, o alejando al inglés del área… o las dos cosas. Pero ese talle de avispa que supone el 4-2-4 tendrá que engordar en los días grandes.

articles.title: El Betis afronta el cierre de mercado pendiente de Ceballos y las salidas
articles.standfirst: Ayer acordó la cesión de Petit; trabaja en la de Losada y otra venta para hacer sitio al utrerano
articles.summary: Ayer acordó la cesión de Petit; trabaja en la de Losada y otra venta para hacer sitio al utrerano
articles.body: Horas frenéticas las que se prepara para vivir hoy el Betis, con varias operaciones sobre la mesa antes de que a las doce de la noche quede cerrado mercado veraniego de fichajes. Ayer, en el día marcado para las salidas, sólo pudo concretar al 100% la de Gonzalo Petit al Cádiz como cedido, que se oficializará este martes. Pero avanzó en otros movimientos con los que hacer sitio a nuevas incorporaciones, con un nombre prioritario encima de la mesa del director deportivo Manu Fajardo: el de Dani Ceballos. El utrerano, después de desvincularse del Real Madrid hace casi dos meses, ha esperado pacientemente para cumplir su deseo de volver al Betis. Ya durante el fin de semana hubo contactos entre el club verdiblanco y la agencia que representa al centrocampista. Unas conversaciones que continuaron ayer, para que Dani conociera de primera mano la situación. El club trabaja en varias salidas no solo para generar espacio salarial suficiente para su incorporación sino también para abrir un hueco en un centro del campo con 'overbooking'. La llave puede estar en el asturiano Álvaro Fidalgo, que cuenta con varias propuestas de equipos de Primera división para salir. Mientras el internacional por México se lo piensa, el Betis acelera también la salida como cedido de Losada, con equipos de Segunda y extranjeros interesados (a la espera de algún primera) y sigue teniendo sobre la mesa los posibles traspasos de Pablo García, que mira a la Premier, y Nelson Deossa, reticente por el momento a abandonar el club pese al deseo de la entidad de recuperar la inversión que realizó en su fichaje. Dani Ceballos ha ido rechazando o aparcando durante todo el verano los distintos ofrecimientos que le han llegado para centrarse únicamente en el Betis. Como agente libre, no necesita que su fichaje se cierre hoy mismo, podría hacerse más adelante si el club genera espacio salarial y fichas disponibles. Pero la lista de la Champions debe quedar remitida a la UEFA mañana, por lo que el movimiento, de concretarse, debe ser en menos de 48 horas. Pellegrini pidió un centrocampista posicional, habrá que ver cómo avanza la operación salida para comprobar si, además del interés por Ceballos, el Betis activa alguna otra incorporación... Mientras sus agentes hablan con el Betis para dar forma a un contrato que sólo se activaría si los verdiblancos consiguen hacerle sitio en su margen salarial y su plantilla, el utrerano ha compartido una llamativa publicación en su perfil social de Instagram, con una fotografía de una iglesia y un mensaje: "Confío en ti, Dios". Ceballos aguarda el desenlace de un regreso a casa por el que lleva tiempo peleando y que ahora está en manos del club andaluz.

articles.title: Jack Grealish transfer: Everton agree loan deal with Man City for England midfielder
articles.summary: Everton agree a deal for Jack Grealish to return to the club on a season-long loan from Manchester City.
articles.body:
Everton have agreed a deal for Jack Grealish to return to the club on a season-long loan from Manchester City .

The 30-year-old is set for a medical at the Toffees, with his move expected to be completed before Tuesday's 23:00 BST transfer deadline.

Grealish spent a large chunk of last term at Everton under a similar arrangement, scoring twice and providing six assists in 20 appearances, before sustaining a season-ending foot injury in January.

The England winger had been linked with other teams - including his boyhood club Aston Villa - but his preference was to return to Everton , whose chief executive Angus Kinnear told BBC Radio Merseyside had "remained in contact" with Grealish.

With Toffees winger Iliman Ndiaye, 26, expected to complete a £65m switch to City , the Merseyside club want to bolster their attacking options before the deadline.

Everton also look to be closing in on the signing of Monaco and USA forward Folarin Balogun in a £40m deal.

However, their bid to re-sign Brazil striker Richarlison from Tottenham appears to have stalled over personal terms.

Grealish, who joined City from Villa for £100m in August 2021, has made two appearances for Enzo Maresca's side this season.

He came on as a substitute in their Community Shield defeat by Arsenal before coming off the bench in a win against Bournemouth in their Premier League opener.

Grealish did not figure in a 4-1 victory at Crystal Palace on Friday.

Meanwhile, Everton 's Scotland defender Nathan Patterson could move to Serie A side Torino before Tuesday's transfer deadline.

Talks are under way between the clubs about a deal for the 24-year-old. It is not yet clear whether any transfer would be on loan or a permanent move.

Everton are next in action on Sunday, when they host Manchester United in the Premier League (14:00 BST).

articles.title: Renovar a Remiro y Oyarzabal, próximos objetivos de Aperribay: “La Real es la casa de Mikel para toda la vida”
articles.standfirst: El presidente del club txuriurdin tiene negociaciones pendientes con el portero y el campeón del Mundo, cuyos contratos terminan en 2027 y 2028, respectivamente
articles.summary: El presidente del club txuriurdin tiene negociaciones pendientes con el portero y el campeón del Mundo, cuyos contratos terminan en 2027 y 2028, respectivamente
articles.body: Jokin Aperribay dejó entrever con bastante claridad, en la rueda de prensa que la Real Sociedad ofreció para presentar a Mamadou Sarr y Héctor Fort, que las renovaciones de Mikel Oyarzabal y Álex Remiro son dos de sus objetivos a nivel de despacho para la temporada 2026-27. Aperribay mostró su deseo de ampliar el contrato que Oyarzabal tiene para sólo dos cursos más poco después de decir que un futbolista no quiso escuchar una gran oferta que llegó por él, pero no quiso dar el nombre, aunque muchos pensamos en el campeón del Mundo. “Han llegado ofertas, alguna me ha sorprendido, porque recibí la llamada directamente, y el jugador se ha cerrado en banda a tener conversaciones sobre traspasos. ¿Oyarzabal? No voy a dar nombres de jugadores”. Después se le cuestionó por esa negociación pendiente con el capitán txuriurdin, que se ha quedado con uno de los contratos más cortos y antiguos de la plantilla. “No hemos hablado, pero Oyarzabal sabe que esta es su casa los próximos dos años y, sinceramente, creo que para toda la vida”. Aperribay se manejó tan bien en la rueda de prensa que cuando concluía se permitió hacerse una pregunta a él mismo para hablar de Remiro, cuyo futuro también ha sido un tema durante el verano. “Y no me preguntáis por Álex Remiro, pero es otra de las personas con las que también hablaremos sobre su renovación. Es un portero que ha dado muchísimo a la Real Sociedad y no tenemos ninguna intención de que se vaya. Ojalá pueda estar aquí muchos años”. El presidente txuriurdin, por tanto, anticipó al valorar el mercado de verano de la Real posiblemente dos de sus mayores objetivos para el otoño e invierno, que es ampliar el contrato de Remiro, que finaliza el próximo 30 de junio, y también el de Oyarzabal, que siendo el mejor futbolista no renueva desde 2023, lo que convierte su documento en uno de los más antiguos, aunque parece evidente que su sueldo sí habrá sido mejorado desde entonces, por el gran rendimiento que viene ofreciendo.

articles.title: La sexta vida de Camavinga
articles.standfirst: El francés, uno de los que Mourinho decidió no dejar salir, gana peso a base de trabajo y ya se ha ganado un elogio público del técnico
articles.summary: El francés, uno de los que Mourinho decidió no dejar salir, gana peso a base de trabajo y ya se ha ganado un elogio público del técnico
articles.body: Camavinga aún tiene cosas que decir. El francés afronta su sexta temporada en el Real Madrid con mucho que demostrar, y lo hace después de un verano en el que su continuidad llegó a cuestionarse. Tras un curso muy flojo, su nombre sonó entre los que podían salir para aliviar la caja, pero él nunca contempló hacer las maletas, y la llegada de Mourinho al banquillo terminó de despejar cualquier duda. El luso le dio hueco en su plantilla, y esa confianza es, hoy, su punto de partida para reivindicarse. Su verano, eso sí, arrancó con mal pie. Se quedó fuera de la lista de Didier Deschamps para el Mundial que Francia cerró en un discreto cuarto puesto. La ausencia le permitió incorporarse antes a la pretemporada y convertirse en uno de los alumnos aventajados de Mou en un mediocampo huérfano de efectivos. Eduardo fue titular en tres de los cuatro amistosos, esperando desde el banquillo únicamente en el último. Las sensaciones, no obstante, fueron intermitentes. El francés alternaba tramos buenos con otros más desalentadores dentro de un mismo encuentro, un vaivén que alimentaba las dudas sobre su rendimiento. La tónica cambió ante el Málaga, en un partido de calado positivo, con apenas unos fallos contados, en el que por fin ofreció el nivel que se le venía exigiendo. El punto de inflexión que necesitaba. Y en ese renacer, Mourinho tiene buena parte de la culpa. El técnico le echó un capote tras el duelo ante los malaguistas, con un elogio significativo. "Camavinga, un chico que no es muy amado, ha hecho un partidazo. Estoy muy contento con la respuesta que ha dado", declaró el luso en rueda de prensa. Porque en una plantilla que se quedará prácticamente como está, el francés dispondrá de más oportunidades de las que cualquiera habría estimado al término de la pasada campaña. Los relevos del verano se han producido hombre por hombre —Bernardo Silva llegó en el lugar de Ceballos—, sin engordar la nómina de centrocampistas, de modo que el reparto de minutos deja hueco para todos. Con ese panorama, el galo debe optimizar su mayor argumento, el de contar con unas prestaciones diferentes al resto. Su capacidad para cubrir metros, robar y salir conduciendo lo convierten en un perfil necesario. Si logra sostener la versión que asomó ante el Málaga, Camavinga tiene con qué reinventarse en un soldado de Mou desde el segundo plano, uno de esos futbolistas que el luso siempre ha sabido rentabilizar.

articles.title: Nick Woltemade: Juventus agree to sign Newcastle forward on loan
articles.summary: Juventus agree a season-long loan deal for Newcastle United forward Nick Woltemade.
articles.body:
Juventus have agreed a season-long loan deal for Newcastle United forward Nick Woltemade.

The Italian side had been one of a number of clubs from the continent interested in signing the 24-year-old before Tuesday's deadline.

Woltemade - brought to Newcastle from Stuttgart in August 2025 - is now set to travel to Turin for a medical after a £3.5m deal was struck. It does not include an option to make it permanent.

Although Woltemade came off the bench to set up Yoane Wissa's goal in Newcastle 's 2-0 win at Tottenham Hotspur on Saturday, the club's £69m record signing has only started one of new manager Matthias Jaissle's first three games to date.

Juventus had been in the market for a forward as Jonathan David looks set to join Atletico Madrid on loan.

They had also been talking to Manchester United striker Joshua Zirkzee, whose proposed move to Fiorentina was not completed.

However, Juventus feel Woltemade is a better fit and, crucially, is also cheaper. In addition, the loan agreement does not include the obligation-to-buy clause Manchester United wanted with Zirkzee.

BBC Sport previously reported that Newcastle 's move for Lille forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo could pave the way for Woltemade to join the Serie A side.

Fernandez-Pardo flew into Tyneside on Monday evening to finalise a move worth up to £55m.

articles.title: Messi retires from international football: ‘Eternal’ star praised by peers
articles.summary: Messi retires as one of the greatest players of all time after a glittering and decades-long career for Argentina.
articles.body:
The football world has paid homage to Argentina’s “eternal” superstar Lionel Messi following his decision to retire from the national team aged 39.

Argentina’s record appearance maker and scorer, with 125 goals in 207 games, said on Monday the decision to end his international career “still hurts deep down” but that “the time has come.”

After the death of his father, Jorge, last month, Messi had said he had “ serious doubts ” about continuing to play football of any sort for “much longer”.

Angel Di Maria, who played alongside Messi in their FIFA 2022 World Cup triumph in Qatar , said it was “so hard” to know fans will not be able to see the talismanic forward in the sky blue and white colours of Argentina any more.

“I only know that I was born in the right century to be able to see you, enjoy you, and on top of that, to share all these years with you on the national team,” added Di Maria.

Rodrigo De Paul, Messi’s Argentinian teammate at his Major League Soccer club Inter Miami, applauded the record eight-time Ballon d’Or winner’s “unconditional love” for the country.

“Just thank you, the greatest of all time, thank you for making us so, so happy, you can’t imagine how many smiles you brought!!” he added.

Argentina midfielder Enzo Fernandez said it would be hard to imagine the next training camp without Messi, who also led them to this year’s World Cup final in North America.

“Stepping onto the pitch and not seeing you up front, wearing the number 10. I’ve spent so many years seeing you there that it seems impossible to imagine it any other way,” he added.

Fellow forward Lautaro Martinez felt there were not “enough words” to thank Messi for his service for the country, for whom he debuted in 2005.

“Beyond everything you achieved on the pitch, what stays with me is everything you taught us off it: Never to give up, to keep trying after every setback, to work quietly and, above all, to always believe in ourselves,” Martinez said.

“We’re going to miss you so much, captain. We’ll be eternally grateful to have been able to share this journey with you. Thank you for everything, captain!”

Apart from his national teammates, Messi also drew tributes from Argentinian President Javier Milei, who called the diminutive player an “incredible man”, while the country’s football association chief Claudio Tapia labelled him “the captain of our dreams”.

“That kid, ‘La Pulga’, that alien who made possible what so often seemed impossible… You are already a legend of this land, of our national team and of world football,” said Tapia.

“You made us believe in magic. And perhaps that’s why we find it hard to accept that time marches on for you too. The Argentina national team shirt is your flag. And our people’s love for you will last forever.”

FIFA President Gianni Infantino congratulated Messi on his glittering career, adding that the Argentinian brought “so much joy to millions of fans”.

“You are retiring from international football as a FIFA World Cup champion and as one of the greatest players our sport has ever seen. I wish you all the best,” said Infantino.

The tributes were not limited to the football world, with Argentinian Formula One driver Franco Colapinto, who drives for the Alpine F1 Team, also thanking Messi.

“We are lucky to have had you and enjoyed [watching you play] for so long,” he said. “Thank you for getting back up time and time again and giving everything to make an entire country happy. You are an example to all of us.”

Antonela Roccuzzo, Messi’s wife, also showered praise, saying, “What a privilege to have been by your side on this journey and to see you fulfil all your dreams.

“You deserved this story and so much more. We love you infinitely,” she added.

articles.title: Ex-NFL star Colin Kaepernick’s unfinished business
articles.summary: Ten years after taking a knee to stand against racism and police brutality at great cost to his career and finances, Colin Kaepernick is back in the spotlight.
articles.body: Colin Kaepernick still puts in a workout at 4:30 a.m. most days. His football life may be long over, but his life’s work is not. Ten years after taking a knee to stand against racism and police brutality at great cost to his career and finances, the former star quarterback is stepping back into the spotlight. His memoir, “The Perilous Fight,” comes out on Sept. 15. And in interviews with NBC News, his first time speaking in depth about his protest’s fallout in years, Kaepernick reveals the story behind how he came to take a knee in 2016, an act that made him both a hero and a pariah, and one of the most divisive figures in the country. Kaepernick, 38, is now also a father to a 4-year-old girl. That, he says, helped him understand he has unfinished business in his life and cause. Being a dad “increases the responsibility and urgency of the work we’re doing,” he says. He doesn’t want his daughter — or anyone else — to think he stopped fighting or that the fight was not worth it. “I don’t want my community to watch me and have the takeaway be that if you fight for Black folks, it’s over for you,” he writes in his book. Much has shifted in American politics, culture, sports and policing since 2016. And much work still needs to be done, Kaepernick says, which is why he chose now to recount the decade-long odyssey that began with a quiet protest during the national anthem. Though the years have provided perspective, Kaepernick says they haven’t dulled his displeasure with the NFL. The quarterback who once led the San Francisco 49ers on a Disney movie-esque run to the Super Bowl in 2012 says he hasn’t watched an NFL game since he was exiled from the league. “I’m not gonna support an organization that one, is actively blackballing me, but two, has targeted my brothers who have been protesting as part of this as well,” Kaepernick says. “I watch college football.” (NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell has said on multiple occasions he doesn’t believe Kaepernick was blackballed.) On Sept. 1, 2016, Kaepernick and his San Francisco 49ers teammate Eric Reid took a knee during the national anthem before a preseason game. It was not the first time Kaepernick didn’t stand. His protest actually began a month earlier, on Aug. 14, when he sat on the bench during “The Star-Spangled Banner.” The idea had simmered in the months prior to the season when, he writes in his memoir, he was recuperating from surgeries. He might not have taken a knee if he hadn’t injured it first. The rehab gave him more free time than he ever had in his life. And in the midst of news of police violence, Kaepernick immersed himself in literature on Black liberation, reading books such as “The Autobiography of Malcolm X” and “Black Skin, White Masks” by Frantz Fanon. Kaepernick says he hadn’t planned the initial protest in mid-August until he heard the opening of the anthem and felt he couldn’t bring himself to stand. No one seemed to notice him sitting at first. It wasn’t until after the 49ers’ third preseason game that Kaepernick was finally asked why he sat out the anthem. “I am not going to stand up to show pride in a flag for a country that oppresses Black people and people of color,” Kaepernick told NFL Network’s Steve Wyche. “To me, this is bigger than football and it would be selfish on my part to look the other way. There are bodies in the street and people getting paid leave and getting away with murder.” Kaepernick was unprepared for the response, he writes in the book. After the game, he called his partner, Nessa, and mentioned the reporter’s question. “Hmm. Well, what did you tell him?” she asked. “On a scale of one to 10, with 10 being the worst, how hard did you go?” “I don’t know. Maybe a four,” Kaepernick replied. The backlash was immediate. Fans burned his jerseys. Current and former players said he disrespected the flag. Donald Trump, then a presidential candidate, said Kaepernick “should find a country that works better for him.” “This is not a four, man,” Kaepernick recalls Nessa telling him when the news blew up. Even though the story of the protest has been told countless times since 2016, Kaepernick set the record straight on one key detail: who came up with the idea to kneel in the first place. Before the Sept. 1 game, Kaepernick was approached by Reid, who wanted to support the protest. It was Reid who suggested the idea to kneel, Kaepernick says. Not Army veteran Nate Boyer, as was widely reported at the time and since. Boyer, a Green Beret and former Seattle Seahawk, had penned an open letter to Kaepernick in the Army Times, writing: “Even though my initial reaction to your protest was one of anger, I’m trying to listen to what you’re saying and why you’re doing it.” On the day of the game, Boyer met with Kaepernick and Reid and relayed stories about how veterans responded to his open letter. The conversation, Boyer says, then shifted to how the protest could be respectful of the military. “I think it was Colin specifically that asked it. He said, ‘Well, do you think there’s a way that we could protest that’s not going to offend people in the military?’” Boyer recalls. “And I said, ‘No. No matter what, some people will be offended.’” Boyer then told Kaepernick he believed sitting on the bench “wasn’t the most inspiring” and that the protest could be more effective if he was next to his teammates, perhaps bowing his head while standing. “He said no immediately, and I respect that,” Boyer says, and the conversation then logically turned to taking a knee. He doesn’t dispute that the two players may have come to that conclusion before meeting him. “I remember them nodding their heads and looking at each other,” Boyer says. “Maybe Eric did suggest that, and that’s kind of what that look was.” After the Sept. 1 game, Reid told reporters “[Boyer] agreed with” the idea for them to kneel. Kaepernick says the notion it was Boyer’s idea appealed to the media because the backing of a white military veteran made the protest seem more “palatable.” As for why Kaepernick didn’t clear up the misconception at the time, he says he and Reid wanted to focus on their message, not get caught “in a personal back-and-forth over whose idea it was.” Though Kaepernick and Reid ultimately switched from sitting to kneeling, the protest continued to stoke controversy. Then-Supreme Court Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg called it “dumb and disrespectful.” Even Kaepernick’s adoptive parents initially said it was “disgraceful.” Along with the backlash, there was also a groundswell of support from the people he was protesting for, as well as athletes from other sports who joined the effort. “Oftentimes we hear a lot of the side of the pushback, but I think what’s disconnected from a lot of that is actually the response directly in communities that we were seeing, and the momentum and the excitement around the effort of no, we’re actually going to change this,” Kaepernick told NBC News during a recent sit-down. Those who condemned his protest chose to focus on his kneeling during the anthem — as opposed to the police violence that drove him to do it. “The critique of the method is a way to distract from the actual message,” Kaepernick says. “The conversation that was being had is taking a knee is more problematic than Black people being killed. Just simply put, ‘Hey, we need to talk about taking a knee. This is urgent. We need to resolve this.’ But another Black person gets killed, and it’s like, ‘Oh well, that’s kind of normal.’” In most of the coverage, Kaepernick’s assertion rang true. The conversation stuck to the red, white and blue, and not the disproportionate number of Black Americans killed by police that the quarterback tried to bring attention to. As Kaepernick tried desperately to keep his protest on message, the rest of his life was picked apart, from his romantic partner to his clothing choices. When Kaepernick revealed he didn’t vote in the 2016 election, ESPN’s Stephen A. Smith called him “irrelevant” and a “flaming hypocrite.” Reaction from players was also mixed. While Reid, Kaepernick and five other players kneeled in Week 1 of the 2016 season, many who said they were sympathetic to Kaepernick’s cause disagreed with his decision not to stand for the anthem. There was a group chat with roughly 100 players from all 32 teams that often grew contentious. In his memoir, Kaepernick writes of a text exchange in September 2016 in which then-Seahawks cornerback Richard Sherman told him he shouldn’t tell players how to protest. (Through his podcast producer, Sherman declined to comment.) The tension in the group chat was palpable, one former player in the chat who spoke on condition of anonymity tells NBC News. Some suggested Kaepernick was only kneeling for personal gain, even though by then it was clear he’d suffer a professional blow. In 2017, he became a free agent after the 49ers told him they would release him. The summer passed, and beyond a meeting with the Seattle Seahawks, no teams scheduled workouts. “I thoroughly enjoyed meeting with Colin, we just didn’t get to the next level,” then-Seahawks coach Pete Carroll wrote NBC News in an email about the meeting. Kaepernick says his meeting with Carroll and general manager John Schneider focused on his political beliefs. (The Seahawks did not respond to a request for comment.) “Which, in pretty much any environment outside the NFL, would be immediate litigation,” Kaepernick says. The same league that let Michael Vick play again after he went to prison for dogfighting, and allowed Deshaun Watson to sign a contract for $230 million following accusations of sexual misconduct by over 20 women (Watson has maintained his innocence), was keeping Kaepernick out. “There’s not a definitive moment that I would point to,” Kaepernick says about when he realized what was happening. Instead, it was more of a culmination. “Coming on the back of going to a Super Bowl, going to an NFC Championship, setting records, and not a single team would bring me in, even for a workout?” Kaepernick says. In August 2017, the Miami Dolphins — whose owner Stephen Ross previously launched a nonprofit to fight systemic racism — signed quarterback Jay Cutler after an injury to starter Ryan Tannehill, even though Cutler had already retired. NFL team executives, meanwhile, used the media to try to throw water on the idea that Kaepernick was blackballed. Some coaches and GMs did reach out, Kaepernick says, and explicitly told him, “Yeah, we want to bring you in, but it’s getting shut down above us.” One of those coaches, writes Kaepernick in his book, was John Harbaugh, the then-head coach of the Baltimore Ravens. Kaepernick spoke extensively with Harbaugh during the summer of 2017. Harbaugh’s brother Jim was Kaepernick’s coach during the 49ers’ run to the Super Bowl. Kaepernick writes that Harbaugh was “pushing” to sign him, but was “shut down from above.” In October 2017, Kaepernick filed a grievance against the NFL under the terms of the league’s and players’ collective bargaining agreement, alleging that owners were colluding against signing him due to his protest. “Everybody believes that he was blackballed,” says one former player who was in the league during 2016. “Players knew that this would happen. That was a firm belief around the league.” Goodell pushed back on the notion of organized collusion to keep Kaepernick out of the NFL. “Those are decisions that each individual owner has to make and their clubs, coaches, GMs,” Goodell told NBC in 2020. “And I’ve talked to a lot of our clubs about it and I’ve encouraged them. I’d love to see him play again.” In November 2019 — months after the NFL settled Kaepernick’s lawsuit — the league tried to arrange a midseason workout for him in front of all 32 teams. The details of this day are now infamous, as Kaepernick ultimately called off the NFL’s workout the morning of due to an extensive waiver he refused to sign — a waiver Kaepernick believed would sign away his employment rights and potential future claims — and instead managed to organize a workout of his own. The dissolution of the workout drew another round of skepticism, with many claiming Kaepernick was pulling a media stunt or was not serious about wanting to play again. While Kaepernick was out of the league, the NFL went about trying to turn the temperature down on his protest, battling the aftermath of an especially divisive election and a ratings slide some attributed to the player demonstrations. The league partnered in 2017 with the Players Coalition, a group founded to address systemic racism, and has since committed over half a billion dollars to various social justice causes. Kaepernick wasn’t part of the group. (Reid said in 2017 that Kaepernick was kicked out of communications with the group by co-founder Malcolm Jenkins, which Jenkins denied.) The NFL did whatever it could to stop the kneeling, the former player says, believing the league wanted to weed out players who kneeled: “What happened was the league and the Players Coalition came to a deal, and then the league did what they were going to do … They wanted their games to go back to normal.” Kaepernick’s protest likely cost him tens of millions of dollars, even accounting for whatever he got from the NFL in the settlement. But as his career was sacked, as television pundits continued to make personal attacks, and as 986 people were killed by police in 2017, Kaepernick stayed largely quiet. He says that was by design. “No individual should be speaking for everyone across the country. I don’t think that’s a responsible way to approach things,” Kaepernick says. “It’s also being able to enable other people to step into leadership positions, because that’s what movements actually are. It’s not one person just driving things.” Months after his workout snafu, events unrelated to Kaepernick raised the volume on his protest once more. On May 25, 2020, 46-year-old George Floyd was killed by police officer Derek Chauvin in Minnesota. Video revealed Chauvin kneeled on Floyd’s neck for over nine minutes, killing him. Chauvin was convicted on multiple murder charges in 2021. Nearly four years after Kaepernick kneeled in response to police brutality, worldwide protests emerged in the wake of Floyd’s killing. Kaepernick says seeing the protests around the world made him hopeful in the moment, especially as people in some cases risked their own well-being to be heard in the middle of the pandemic. “There was a significant portion of the population that previously was disconnected from these realities,” Kaepernick says. “It was like, oh, actually I have to sit with this now and I have to grapple with this. And am I OK with this? And what is my role within this? Am I complicit?” Corporations also scrambled to meet the moment, including the NFL. In June 2020, several NFL players coordinated social media posts asking for the league to condemn racism and “admit wrong in silencing our players from peacefully protesting.” The next day, Goodell responded in a video message. “We, the National Football League, condemn racism and the systematic oppression of Black people,” Goodell said in the video, echoing the words players demanded from him. “We, the National Football League, admit we were wrong for not listening to NFL players earlier and encourage all to speak out and peacefully protest. We, the National Football League, believe Black lives matter.” Kaepernick wasn’t impressed. “His response through that video was only because of pressure from players, not because it was altruistic,” Kaepernick says. The idea that the league should have listened to protesting players “is so laughable in my mind, and so disingenuous,” Kaepernick says. “We had been trying to address the issue that the NFL created with blackballing me for years. To come out and say we should have listened on the back of that — while I’m still actively trying to play in the NFL — it’s so performative.” Starting the season after Goodell’s video, the NFL began adding messages such as “Choose Love” and “End Racism” in the end zones of every stadium. It continued donating millions to the Inspire Change fund. In 2021, the league expanded on its Rooney Rule, which requires teams to interview at least two minority candidates for certain jobs. “‘End Racism’ in the back of the end zone is a great marketing campaign, but what are the actions behind it?” Kaepernick says. He adds that at the same time the league was putting slogans on the field, it was employing the practice of “race norming,” arguing that Black players began their careers with lower cognitive function in an effort to deny them payments as a result of a 2013 concussion lawsuit. (The NFL halted the practice in 2021.) “I don’t think the NFL has materially changed. None of their actions show that,” Kaepernick says. “We have seen it time and time again. For them it has gone back to business as usual, and I think that is a tragedy that we have allowed them to be able to get to that point.” In a statement to NBC News, the NFL said: “The issues Colin and other NFL players raised remain important to the league and deserving of continued attention and action,” noting the league still works with Inspire Change to “support meaningful progress.” The NFL added: “Since 2017, that work has reached thousands of national and grassroots partners, backed by more than $575 million in contributions. We remain committed to listening, collaborating, and taking action that creates lasting impact.” While 2020 appeared to cast Kaepernick’s protest in a more favorable light, the country’s collective backlash seemed even more pronounced after Trump was elected to a second term. Many corporations and college campuses rolled back their diversity, equality and inclusion practices. Many politicians disavowed or walked back their anti-police stances from the aftermath of Floyd’s death. Meanwhile, high-profile athletes, including some who supported Kaepernick, have retreated on taking political stances on issues such as the killing of Americans by immigration enforcement agents this year. “We have seen on the corporate side a shift in capitulation to the administration,” Kaepernick says, which he says in turn has had an effect on athletes. In this environment, Kaepernick says he tries to be strategic about when to speak up. “I try not to just flood things and be a stream of consciousness of everything because it does lose some of the impact,” he says. “I try to be intentional. When is it the right time and place for me to speak up on something?” Though his prospects of getting back on the field have dimmed, Kaepernick says he still trains as if he’s in the NFL. His daily routine typically begins with his early morning workout. Then, he says, his real work begins: He helps get his 4-year-old daughter ready for school. He devotes time to his various business endeavors, ranging from the Know Your Rights Camp to his AI company Lumi Story to his production house, Kaepernick Media. Being a father has especially added a new sense of urgency, he says. “You no longer have the luxury of thinking about it from a perspective of, it’s just me going through this world,” he says. “You think about it from the responsibility of creating an environment and a society that allows someone that is like your child to be able to grow up and thrive.” Kaepernick says his approach to politics has also evolved. He’s voted in the last two presidential elections and says he recognizes now that the strategy of not voting wasn’t right. Though still committed to his cause, Kaepernick says he often does his work behind the scenes. His Know Your Rights Camp has helped pay for 150 independent autopsies — such as the one for Nolan Wells this year — and has also paid hundreds of thousands in legal grants and bail relief. In August, Kaepernick pledged another $1 million to community organizations. Even as the country rubber-bands between the hyperactivism of 2020 and the cultural and political backlash since, Kaepernick — after all he’s been through — remains optimistic. “I’m very hopeful when I think about the moment that we are in,” Kaepernick says. Does that mean he feels his legacy is vindicated? “Candidly, I don’t think about legacy a whole lot,” he says. “What I think about is what are the areas that I can do work that I think are going to have an impact and help us move towards that future together. At the end of the day, people will decide what that legacy is, and hopefully that’s a positive one.”

articles.title: Chelsea transfer latest: Deal close for Roma midfielder Manu Kone, as loan explored for Jamie Gittens to go the other way
articles.summary: Chelsea are close to agreeing a deal to sign Manu Kone from Roma; Roma boss Gian Piero Gasperini does not want to sell a player and is seen as an obstacle to overcome; a loan deal for Jamie Gittens to go the other direction is being explored
articles.body:
A deal worth £52m was understood to have been discussed, with talks also advancing to see winger Jamie Gittens head in the other direction on loan.

Kone is being lined up as a replacement for Enzo Fernandez, with talks ongoing over a move to Manchester City for the Argentina international.

Chelsea's negotiations continue for both Kone and Gittens, but Gasperini's reluctance to let Kone go is an obstacle to overcome.

Gapserini pushed for Kone to stay when he arrived as head coach and was instrumental in securing the France midfielder's immediate future there.

Roma are working on either AC Milan midfielder Youssouf Fofana or Marseille's Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg to replace Kone.

Monaco have rejected a £38.5m (€45m) bid from Chelsea for Lamine Camara.

Sky Sports News reported on Friday that Monaco do not want to sell Camara, who has three years left on his contract at the French club.

It would take a massive offer for Monaco to change their stance on the 22-year-old in this transfer window.

It is understood that Monaco have received lots of interest for Camara.

Kone has pedigree as a 19-cap France international who, at 25, and with his peak years still ahead of him, has already impressed in Italy, Germany and his homeland, demonstrating a capacity to adapt which could serve him well in the Premier League.

The former Borussia Monchengladbach midfielder has good athleticism and technical quality. Like the player he is in line to replace at Chelsea, he can operate at both No 6 and No 8, although it is at the base of midfield that he is most comfortable.

That may suit Alonso given his favoured, three-at-the-back system leaves little room for the No 8 role in which Fernandez previously excelled for the club. It may also suit Kone, who can defend, pass and carry but doesn't offer the same level of attacking threat.

Fernandez thrived in that sense at Chelsea. The Argentina international contributed an impressive total of 16 goals and 11 assists in the last two Premier League seasons.

Chelsea might need to find those goals and assists elsewhere in his squad if he goes, with Kone, a player who has different strengths, having provided only two and five respectively in league games for Roma in the same timeframe.

articles.title: Arsenal agree terms to sign defender Elisa de Almeida from PSG
articles.summary: Arsenal agree terms to sign versatile France defender Elisa de Almeida from Paris St-Germain.
articles.body:
Arsenal have agreed terms to sign France defender Elisa de Almeida from Paris St-Germain.

Sources in France suggest the fee could be about £550,000 and she is expected to join before Thursday's transfer deadline.

The versatile 28-year-old can play at centre-back - an area where Arsenal need cover at the start of the season because of injuries.

De Almeida has spent five years at PSG, making more than 100 appearances and has experience of competing in the Women's Champions League.

She has spent her entire career in France, representing Paris FC before a spell at Montpellier, prior to joining PSG.

De Almeida has played 52 games for France and was part of Les Bleues' squads at the 2023 Women's World Cup and Euro 2025.

Arsenal are seeking to win a first Women's Super League title since 2019 and have strengthened this summer, with additions including England midfielder Georgia Stanway and Spain full-back Ona Batlle.

Renee Slegers' side start their season at Brighton on Sunday, 6 September (12:00 BST).

articles.standfirst: El suizo entrena ya con el grupo y apunta a seguir en Nervión; Agoumé, Isaac y Robbie Ure trabajaron en el gimnasio
articles.summary: El suizo entrena ya con el grupo y apunta a seguir en Nervión; Agoumé, Isaac y Robbie Ure trabajaron en el gimnasio
articles.body: El Sevilla arrancó este martes su semana de entrenamientos en la Ciudad Deportiva José Ramón Cisneros Palacios, con el objetivo de preparar la visita al Espanyol del próximo domingo. Durante la mañana, toda la atención mediática estuvo centrada en los posibles movimientos de entradas y salidas, ya que el mercado de fichajes encara sus últimas horas y la entidad hispalense todavía tiene algunas tareas pendientes por resolver. La gran noticia de la jornada la protagonizó Rubén Vargas, que hasta hace unos días estaba a la espera de que Sevilla y Olympiacos pudieran concretar su traspaso. Sin embargo, ambos clubes no lograron un acuerdo económico y la operación se terminó cayendo. Tras una semana convulsa en la que alternó sesiones con el grupo y ejercicios al margen, quedándose fuera de las dos últimas convocatorias, el extremo suizo ha vuelto a entrenar con total normalidad junto a sus compañeros. Un gesto significativo que parece zanjar su culebrón y encarrilar su permanencia en Nervión. La otra nota positiva del entrenamiento corrió a cargo de Marcao. El central brasileño se ejercitó al mismo ritmo que el resto del primer equipo sevillista, encadenando ya varias sesiones consecutivas desde su reaparición la pasada semana. De esta forma confirma su progresiva puesta a punto, dejando atrás sus molestias físicas y estando disponible para Luis García Plaza. La jornada matinal arrancó con una extensa charla inicial de Luis García Plaza a la plantilla. Una vez concluida, Lucien Agoumé, Isaac Romero y Robbie Ure se retiraron del césped para trabajar en el gimnasio. El centrocampista francés arrastra dolor por un fuerte pisotón en el pie derecho, aunque podrá reincorporarse este miércoles a la dinámica grupal. Por su parte, la dupla de atacantes se tomó un respiro a causa de un proceso de faringitis. El Sevilla volverá a ejercitarse este miércoles por la mañana para seguir preparando la cuarta fecha de LaLiga EA Sports. Este domingo, los blanquirrojos buscarán su tercer triunfo del campeonato midiéndose al Espanyol en Cornellá a las 21:00 horas.

articles.title: Alan Knight: Portsmouth's former goalkeeper dies aged 65
articles.summary: Former Portsmouth goalkeeper Alan Knight, who played 801 games for the club, dies aged 65 after being diagnosed with prostate cancer in 2024.
articles.body:
Former Portsmouth goalkeeper Alan Knight has died aged 65 after being diagnosed with prostate cancer in 2024.

Knight spent 22 years playing at Fratton Park, making 801 appearances between 1978 and 2000 – the record for a keeper at a single English club.

Pompey fans gave him the nickname 'The Legend' and after retiring he became both a coach and ambassador for the club.

Knight kept a clean sheet on his debut, aged 16, against Rotherham in the old Division Three in 1978 and he went on to represent the club in all four divisions.

There were three promotion-winning campaigns, including a Division Three title success and Pompey's return to top-flight football for the first time in 28 years in the 1986-87 season.

Knight's final appearance for the club came aged 38 on 3 January 2000 in a 2-1 Division One defeat at Norwich, making him the only Blues player to have played across four decades.

Knight was awarded an MBE following his retirement, and was also handed the Freedom of the City of Portsmouth.

Speaking to the BBC following his cancer diagnosis, Knight said it "came as a massive shock" but he wanted to discuss it publicly to encourage others to seek advice if they spot symptoms.

He joined a group of men playing walking football in Portsmouth and said it helped them all come to terms with their diagnoses.

"Once you get diagnosed, once the cancer word is used, it just changes everything," he said.

"The support network, having your mates around you - family first and foremost - but then to have your mates and your team-mates around you is huge.

"It gives you that lift when you can be slipping into that bit of depression."

articles.title: Matias Fernandez-Pardo to Newcastle: Signing from Lille is 'very fast' with 'unbelievable power' like Jeremy Doku
articles.summary: With Newcastle United signing Matias Fernandez-Pardo for £51m from Lille, Adam Bate speaks to the player's former coach to find out what makes the Belgian forward so good: "You could compare him a little bit to Jeremy Doku. He is very explosive, very fast"
articles.body:
Indeed, Vidarsson, who worked with Fernandez-Pardo at Gent prior to his move to Lille, sees similarities with another Belgian winger who has become a Premier League star. "You could compare him a little bit to Jeremy Doku. They have a similar profile," he says.

"It is that power, that speed, that ability to go past people without needing space." That Doku trademark of slowing the defender down and then suddenly speeding up? He has it too. "Matias can go past people in one or two metres because of this explosiveness."

The reason why Newcastle have been persuaded to pay £51m to bring the 21-year-old Belgium international to the Premier League is that Fernandez-Pardo has shown that he can bring goals too. He has evolved into more of a forward than a winger.

"In my opinion, his best position is central," says Vidarsson. "That is how he scored most of his goals and how Lille scouted him in his last season with Gent." It happened fast. He made his full league debut in March 2024 and played his last game for the club that August.

A run of eight goals in 11 games did that. "The coach started to use him as a striker. Before that, he had always been on the wing. He made a good decision because Matias started to score a lot. After that spell playing centrally, there was big interest in him."

Vidarsson's relationship with Fernandez-Pardo pre-dates that first-team breakthrough. The Icelandic coach, now working in coach development for FIFA, was responsible for talent management at Gent as well as working with the development squad there.

He remembers a quiet boy, one well supported by his family. "His relationship with his father was strong. His father was all in, basically his assistant, driving him everywhere and taking good care of him. Matias did not talk too much." He came alive on the pitch.

The young Fernandez-Pardo was a wide player for Gent's second team. It was a learning process. "His decision-making on the wing was not always the best," Vidarsson recalls. "That is something that Doku, for example, also had when he was at Anderlecht."

He caveats it by saying this was a few years ago. "Players develop. But he was going past people and not knowing when to cross, when to cut inside, when to go outside, when to find space in behind. And sometimes he did not have the mentality to run for the team."

Vidarsson puts that down to the fact that he had probably outgrown the level and was itching for the first-team opportunity that he soon seized. "That is typical of a young player who was being asked to go from the first team to play for the second team."

The breakthrough came in early 2024 when Gent sold three attacking players for significant sums of money. Malick Fofana and Gift Orban both moved to Lyon. Hugo Cuypers was sold to Chicago Fire. "That freed up the space for Matias to play," he explains.

The rest is history and Fernandez-Pardo earned his own switch that summer. "I think it was a great move for him to go to Lille," says Vidarsson. After a promising first season adjusting to the level, he played a key role in qualifying Lille for the Champions League.

Given that achievement, there is some surprise within football that Fernandez-Pardo has been so keen to leave. Certainly, there is a feeling that playing a season of Champions League football with the French club would have aided his development.

Vidarsson himself preaches caution in expecting too much on Tyneside, at least in the short term. "I would say they are taking, not a risk, but let's say giving him an opportunity," he says, rather diplomatically. This is another step up for him, after all.

"He has the potential but I really do believe that he will need one season to adapt before he can shine and become a top player in the Premier League. Because everything in the Premier League is faster, more intense. Everything there happens at a faster tempo."

There is a belief that Matthias Jaissle's vertical style of play could suit Fernandez-Pardo - if he is used in the channel rather than just stuck out on the wing. "It will probably always be better for Matias to play in a system as one of two strikers," argues Vidarsson.

"Because of his speed, he needs space. On the wing, you can direct him in one direction and then he becomes a little easier to mark." That might change, of course. In part, because he can "grow into a bigger club, into a bigger environment" at Newcastle.

The World Cup felt like a missed opportunity as Fernandez-Pardo was restricted to just three appearances off the bench for Belgium. Tired of waiting, he has pushed for the club move that he craved and the chance now to play in the Premier League.

There is much to learn and much to prove. But Newcastle supporters have reason to be excited. Not because Fernandez-Pardo is the finished article, but because he isn't. And because he possesses that one quality that means he always has the capacity to excite.

"What he has, of course, is that special thing that a lot of clubs are looking for in modern football, that speed, that ability to go past people and do something in small spaces. He has those attributes and they are really difficult to create. You are just born with it."
