articles.title: B/R's Preseason 2026 College Football Top 20 Quarterback Rankings
articles.summary: Welcome to Bleacher Report's first quarterback rankings of the 2026 college football season.
articles.body:
Welcome to Bleacher Report's first quarterback rankings of the 2026 college football season.

With Fernando Mendoza, Diego Pavia, Ty Simpson, Haynes King and Carson Beck among the notable high-profile quarterbacks who have departed the college ranks since last season, the QB1 landscape has a new look, albeit with plenty of familiar faces.

Past performance, physical projection, level of competition and supporting cast all played a part in determining where each quarterback fell in our preseason rankings, but once the season starts, the focus will be solely on 2026 production.

If your favorite team's quarterback is not currently in the top 20, he will inevitably find his way into the rankings if he's putting up numbers. Our Top 20 list will be updated every Tuesday morning throughout the season. That's the beauty of a weekly staple!

Passing: 300-of-454, 66.1 cmp%, 3,641 yards, 26 TD, 13 INT Rushing: 71 carries, 55 yards, 4 TD

With back-to-back 3,000-yard, 20-touchdown seasons under his belt and a trip to the College Football Playoff in 2024, Kevin Jennings returns to SMU as one of the most experienced quarterbacks in the nation.

His ACC-leading 13 interceptions and the dip in his rushing production from 354 to 55 yards cap his upside a bit relative to some of the other standouts on this list, but he is 1,373 yards away from becoming SMU's all-time leading passer.

Passing: 232-of-356, 65.2 cmp%, 2,705 yards, 25 TD, 9 INT Rushing: 171 carries, 700 yards, 11 TD

Conner Weigman was a 5-star recruit out of high school and the No. 2 quarterback in the 2022 class, slotted between Cade Klubnik (Clemson) and Ty Simpson (Alabama).

He appeared in 15 games and made 13 starts over three seasons at Texas A&M, but missed time due to injuries before finally breaking out after transferring to Houston last year.

Weigman joined Diego Pavia, Arch Manning and Byrum Brown as the only quarterbacks with 25 passing touchdowns and 10 rushing touchdowns.

18. Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele, California

Passing: 316-of-492, 64.2 cmp%, 3,454 yards, 18 TD, 9 INT Rushing: 60 carries, -120 yards, 4 TD

Originally an Oregon recruit and the No. 7 quarterback in the 2025 class, Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele flipped to Cal after last year's quarterback carousel saw Dante Moore go from UCLA to Oregon and Fernando Mendoza from Cal to Indiana.

He took his lumps as a freshman, but flashed legitimate superstar upside in November road wins over Louisville (30-of-47, 323 yards, 2 TD) and SMU (31-of-40, 330 yards, 4 TD) while leading the Golden Bears to their first winning season since 2019.

Passing: 246-of-354, 69.5 cmp%, 3,065 yards, 25 TD, 8 INT Rushing: 143 carries, 611 yards, 6 TD

Demond Williams Jr. had five games last season where he recorded at least four total touchdowns, and he ultimately led Washington to a 9-4 season and a victory in the LA Bowl over Boise State.

However, he also had a few notable duds along the way, including a combined 335 total yards with zero touchdowns and three interceptions in lopsided losses to Ohio State and Michigan. There is no question the talent is there, but he needs to find a bit more consistency against quality competition.

Passing: 234-of-377, 62.1 cmp%, 3,169 yards, 25 TD, 12 INT Rushing: 104 carries, 493 yards, 6 TD

While he has been turnover-prone at times, it's difficult to ignore the fact that Marcel Reed is 15-6 as a starter at Texas A&M, including an 11-0 start last season that ended with a trip to the College Football Playoff.

With road games against LSU, Missouri and Alabama on the schedule this season, he will be tested, and he has the raw talent to take a step forward and emerge as one of the nation's elite quarterbacks in 2026.

Passing: 247-of-397, 62.2 cmp%, 2,885 yards, 14 TD, 11 INT

With 1,215 passing yards, 190 rushing yards and 11 total touchdowns through his first four games last season, John Mateer emerged as one of the early Heisman Trophy front-runners before suffering a broken bone in his throwing hand on Sept. 20 against Auburn.

He missed just one game, but returned with a three-interception performance against Texas on Oct. 11 and completed 59.4 percent of his passes with eight touchdowns and eight interceptions the rest of the way.

With that injury now behind him, can Mateer return to Heisman Trophy candidate form in 2026?

Passing: 145-of-239, 60.7 cmp%, 1,628 yards, 10 TD, 3 INT Rushing: 73 carries, 306 yards, 5 TD

The 2025 stats don't tell the full story with Sam Leavitt, as his redshirt sophomore season at Arizona State was cut short by season-ending foot surgery in early November.

However, he led the Sun Devils to a Big 12 championship and a spot in the College Football Playoff the previous season when he threw for 2,885 yards with 24 touchdowns and six interceptions, while also adding 443 rushing yards and five more scores.

That's the player Lane Kiffin rolled out the red carpet for to headline his LSU transfer class.

Passing: 275-of-428, 64.3 cmp%, 3,228 yards, 29 TD, 6 INT Rushing: 114 carries, 216 yards, 3 TD

A 3-star recruit out of high school with an undersized 5'10" frame, Noah Fifita is on track to leave the University of Arizona as the most prolific passer in school history.

His 73 career passing touchdowns already sit atop the leaderboard, while his 9,183 passing yards are comfortably within striking distance of Nick Foles (10,011) and Willie Tuitama (9,211). He bounced back nicely from a down year in 2024, and the team followed suit with a leap from 4-8 to 9-4.

Passing: 319-of-463, 68.9 cmp%, 4,379 yards, 34 TD, 9 INT Rushing: 57 carries, 89 yards, 5 TD

After leading the nation in passing yards (4,379) and trailing only Heisman Trophy winner Fernando Mendoza in passing touchdowns (34) while piloting the high-powered North Texas offense last season, Drew Mestemaker followed head coach Eric Morris to Oklahoma State.

The former walk-on has come a long way in a very short time, and he will be put to the test early this season with a home game against Oregon on Sept. 12. Win or lose, a strong showing in that game would solidify his status as one of the top passers in the country.

Passing: 272-of-413, 65.9 cmp%, 3,472 yards, 29 TD, 13 INT Rushing: 55 carries, 4 yards, 2 TD

Fernando Mendoza was a productive quarterback rarely mentioned among the nation's top tier before he transferred to Indiana and won the Heisman Trophy last season. Can Josh Hoover follow a similar trajectory?

With 9,629 passing yards and 71 touchdowns across three seasons as the starter at TCU, he is one of the most experienced quarterbacks in the country heading into 2026. He can push the ball downfield, evidenced by his Big 12-leading 8.4 yards per attempt last year, but he also ranked third nationally with 13 interceptions. Curt Cignetti's quarterback development skills will be put to the test.

Passing: 226-of-341, 66.3 cmp%, 3,158 yards, 28 TD, 7 INT Rushing: 175 carries, 1,008 yards, 14 TD

Byrum Brown turned in just the 13th season in college football history with 3,000 passing yards and 1,000 rushing yards last season, and he also showed he's capable of producing against quality competition with victories over then-No. 25 Boise State and then-No. 13 Florida to open the year.

He followed head coach Alex Golesh to Auburn and will now get an opportunity to see if his dual-threat production translates to the SEC. After racking up 42 total touchdowns in 2025, second only to Heisman winner Fernando Mendoza (48), he has the talent to put a team on his back.

Passing: 269-of-386, 69.7 cmp%, 2,894 yards, 24 TD, 5 INT

A 4-star recruit and the No. 7 quarterback in the 2022 class, Gunner Stockton spent his first two collegiate seasons behind Carson Beck on the Georgia depth chart, but he finally stepped into the starting role last year and put together a productive season.

He turned in one of his best performances of the season against Alabama in the SEC championship game (20-of-26, 156 yards, 3 TD), and had four passing touchdowns and one rushing score in both the Ole Miss and Texas games.

Stockton consistently delivered in high-leverage games, an important trait in the SEC.

Passing: 212-of-334, 63.5 cmp%, 2,490 yards, 24 TD, 5 INT Rushing: 146 carries, 835 yards, 10 TD

After racking up 2,768 passing yards, 1,166 rushing yards and 31 total touchdowns during the 2024 season at New Mexico, Devon Dampier transferred to Utah last season and developed into a more well-rounded passer.

His completion percentage (57.9% to 63.5%), yards per attempt (7.1 to 7.5), interception rate (3.1% to 1.5%) and passer rating (121.6 to 146.8) all improved significantly despite the leap in competition.

New head coach Morgan Scalley convinced him to stick around after Kyle Whittingham took the Michigan job, which speaks volumes in today's transfer-centric culture.

Passing: 195-of-293, 66.6 cmp%, 2,741 yards, 24 TD, 6 INT Rushing: 41 carries, 33 yards, 3 TD

With Jeremiah Love anchoring a rushing attack that averaged more than 200 yards per game, Notre Dame didn't need CJ Carr to shoulder the offensive load last year, and he attempted more than 30 passes just five times in 12 games.

That said, his 9.4 yards per attempt ranked third in the nation, and he had multiple passing touchdowns nine times, including a 354-yard, four-touchdown explosion on the road against Arkansas. With more offensive responsibility falling on the passing game now, he has a lot of room to improve on last year's numbers.

Passing: 265-of-403, 65.8 cmp%, 3,711 yards, 24 TD, 10 INT Rushing: 54 carries, 157 yards, 6 TD

After splitting time with Miller Moss in 2024, Jayden Maiava entered last season as USC's unquestioned starting quarterback and ended up leading the Big Ten in passing yards (3,711) while garnering some early Heisman Trophy buzz with nine touchdowns and zero interceptions during the Trojans' 4-0 start.

He will be without All-American wide receiver Makai Lemon (79 catches, 1,156 yards, 11 TD) after he was selected No. 20 overall in this year's draft, but he has the arm talent to again be one of the most prolific passers in the country.

Passing: 296-of-412, 71.8 cmp%, 3,565 yards, 30 TD, 10 INT Rushing: 73 carries, 156 yards, 2 TD

Dante Moore has the talent and upside to be the first quarterback off the board in the 2027 draft, but that doesn't necessarily mean he's the best college signal-caller heading into the season.

He still has room to improve his decision-making under pressure, evidenced by his 10 interceptions last season, and he came away with a lackluster performance in both of his games against eventual national champion Indiana.

His completion percentage (71.8, fourth), passing touchdowns (30, sixth) and passer rating (163.7, eighth) all ranked in the top 10 nationally last year, and his decision to return to campus immediately vaulted Oregon into the national title conversation.

Passing: 334-of-500, 66.8 cmp%, 3,973 yards, 34 TD, 6 INT Rushing: 59 carries, -32 yards, 1 TD

From Tulane in 2024 to Duke in 2025 to Miami this season, Darian Mensah has quickly climbed the prestige ladder since exiting the high school ranks as a 2-star recruit in the 2023 class.

His 3,973 passing yards were second in the nation last season, and now he is surrounded by a more talented collection of skill players, including last year's freshman sensation Malachi Toney (109 catches, 1,211 yards, 10 touchdowns).

The Hurricanes also have Mark Fletcher Jr. (1,192 yards, 12 TD) returning to anchor the running game, and that offensive balance should give Mensah ample opportunities to pick apart opposing defenses.

Passing: 248-of-404, 61.4 cmp%, 3,163 yards, 26 TD, 7 INT Rushing: 92 carries, 399 yards, 10 TD

After a rocky start to the season where he looked overmatched against Ohio State and threw two interceptions in a loss to Florida, Arch Manning hit his stride during the second half of the 2025 campaign.

Over his final six games, he completed 62.3 percent of his passes for 1,714 yards with 14 touchdowns and two interceptions, and he added 206 yards and five more scores on the ground.

What's more, the Longhorns went 5-1 during that stretch, handing Texas A&M its first loss before beating Michigan in the Citrus Bowl. Can he pick up where he left off and put together the Heisman-caliber season many were expecting a year ago?

Passing: 301-of-391, 77.0 cmp%, 3,610 yards, 32 TD, 8 INT Rushing: 42 carries, -44 yards, 0 TD

How much of Julian Sayin's production can be attributed to having the nation's most talented wide receiving corps at his disposal?

Regardless of talent level on the outside, it takes a special quarterback to complete 77 percent of his passes in his first year as a starter, and he deservedly finished fourth in 2025 Heisman Trophy balloting.

What's more, Jeremiah Smith is back alongside 5-star freshman Chris Henry Jr., so we don't even need to waste time playing the hypothetical game of what he might be without an elite pass-catching group because he has one around him again.

Passing: 294-of-445, 66.1 cmp%, 3,937 yards, 22 TD, 3 INT Rushing: 133 carries, 527 yards, 8 TD

It was not immediately clear whether Trinidad Chambliss would be taking the field for the 2026 season, but he was ultimately granted a sixth year of eligibility and now stands as one of the Heisman Trophy favorites.

After four years at D-II Ferris State, capped off by a national championship in 2024, Chambliss made the jump to Ole Miss last year. He began the season as backup to Austin Simmons, but got a chance to start in Week 3 against Arkansas and never looked back.

His proven SEC success, ability to extend plays with his legs, strong arm and quick release give him all the necessary tools to be one of the biggest stars of the 2026 college football season.

articles.title: B/R's 2026 Heisman Trophy Rankings Before Week 1
articles.summary: Personal glory typically takes a back seat to team success, but nobody has ever complained about winning a Heisman Trophy, either.
articles.body:
Personal glory typically takes a back seat to team success, but nobody has ever complained about winning a Heisman Trophy, either.

And in 2026, the race should be incredibly fun.

Entering the season, Notre Dame QB CJ Carr and Texas QB Arch Manning are among the most popular names for college football's top individual honor. Many other power-conference quarterbacks are popular early contenders, too.

The voting tide may be turning, though. One non-QB has been a finalist—a top-four finisher—in three straight years, and two receivers stand out this season.

Consider this a personal ranking of how I see the race playing out in 2026. Starting next week, though, the order will steadily shift from a long-term projection to a reflection of actual production.

10-6. Hoover, Stockton, Toney, Manning and Sayin

Previously a three-year starter at TCU, Josh Hoover is set to lead the reigning champions in 2026. He'll have a strong supporting cast at Indiana, which returns a rising star in receiver Charlie Becker and added key transfer Nick Marsh. Indiana's first-half schedule looks awfully favorable, too.

Gunner Stockton quietly finished seventh in Heisman voting last season. While throwing for 2,894 yards and 24 touchdowns to five interceptions, he rushed for 462 yards and 10 more scores. The receiving corps is a question mark, but UGA's projected team success will likely boost Stockton's appeal.

Whether as a receiver, Wildcat QB or returner, Malachi Toney can impact the game in so many ways. As a true freshman, he made 109 receptions for 1,211 yards and 10 touchdowns while adding one rushing and two passing scores. Toney was an essential part of Miami's national runner-up campaign in 2025 and will remain the team's (heavily) featured playmaker this season.

An early favorite, Arch Manning has no shortage of opportunity. He stumbled through the first half of 2025 but improved down the stretch, ending the campaign with 3,562 total yards and accounting for 37 touchdowns. If the Longhorns are legitimate contenders in 2026, Manning will be soundly on the Heisman radar.

Julian Sayin closed the 2025 season on a couple of sour notes, but expectations are plenty high after he was a Heisman finalist. Last year, he posted a 77.0 completion rate—one of the highest marks in FBS history—while throwing for 3,610 yards and 32 touchdowns as a first-time starter. Playing well in marquee games will be vital to Sayin bolstering his candidacy.

The good news? CJ Carr is a tremendous talent.

During his first season leading the offense, he passed for 2,741 yards with 24 scores to six interceptions. Carr, who isn't much of a runner, chipped in three short touchdowns on the ground.

There is a double-edged sword, however. Notre Dame should be outstanding in 2026, largely because of a powerful defense. Team success is always helpful in this conversation. But it's plausible his box-score stats won't be overly impressive in comparison to other candidates, as well.

Still, what a great problem that would be for the Fighting Irish. Carr can become a Heisman-level QB on a championship-worthy roster.

Trinidad Chambliss, on the other hand, is the single-most important reason why Ole Miss is hovering in the national discussion.

Last season, he surged from an accomplished D-II backup to the surprise starter in the SEC. Chambliss racked up 4,464 offensive yards—the No. 2 total in the country—accounted for 30 touchdowns with just three interceptions and propelled the Rebels to the semifinal round of the College Football Playoff.

His follow-up season will be a heck of a test, though.

Ole Miss has a pretty unrelenting schedule, one that includes six preseason Top 25 opponents. Even if the Rebels end around nine or 10 wins, that should put Chambliss in the range of a top-five voting slot.

At his third school in three years, Darian Mensah is a proven commodity. He took Tulane and Duke to a conference championship game in 2024 and 2025, respectively, and celebrated an ACC title last season. Mensah threw for 3,973 yards and 34 touchdowns with Duke.

Now leading Miami's scoring attack, Mensah should be on his best offense yet.

In addition to boasting Toney at receiver, the 'Canes have Cooper Barkate—who posted 1,106 yards as Mensah's top target at Duke. Throw in a few other complementary pieces, and this supporting cast is terrific.

The make-or-break moment for Mensah presumably will be when Miami travels to Notre Dame in November. If the Hurricanes win there and reach the ACC Championship Game, expect to see Mensah in New York as a Heisman finalist.

Oregon has a veteran roster built to compete for a national title with a deep group of skill-position playmakers around Dante Moore. Few teams can match the trio of Evan Stewart, Dakorien Moore and Jeremiah McClellan at receiver.

The offense should be among the best in the country, especially with Moore—who threw for 3,565 yards and 30 touchdowns last year—running the show.

Put simply, there's no excuse for Oregon not to overpower most defenses.

And if the Ducks live up to that billing, Moore should have an impressive, hyper-efficient stat line on a compelling Heisman résumé.

Dating back to 1991—when Desmond Howard struck the pose—just two wideouts have hoisted the Heisman. Travis Hunter's win in 2024, while well-deserved, was a product of him being a star cornerback, too.

For a receiver to snatch this award, he must be nothing short of phenomenal.

Well, that description applies to Jeremiah Smith. Heading into his third season at Ohio State, he's already a two-time All-American. Smith tallied at least 76 catches, 1,200 yards and 12 touchdowns in both previous years.

Not only is Smith undeniably elite, but he should also command more targets after the departure of first-round NFL draft pick Carnell Tate.

Smith is the best player in the country. Ending his college career with a Heisman Trophy would only be fitting.

articles.title: Everton on Transfer Deadline Day Sep 2026 | Maitland-Niles bid made, Leweling, Yilmaz & Keita linked
articles.summary: This could be as busy a deadline day for Everton as we have seen in many years
articles.body:
Per The Bobble, Everton have made a low-cost bid for Ainsley Maitland-Niles at Lyon!

Other sources however seem to indicate that the deal is done and the player is traveling this afternoon to the UK for his medical with the Blues.

Fulham are abandoning their pursuit of Andrei Ratiu, and moving on to Sacha Boey of Bayern Munich.

German international winger Jamie Leweling has chosen to stay at VFB Stuttgart, despite the Blues' big bid for him worth €43m including add-ons, with €35m guaranteed.

Everton have told West Ham that Michael Keane is going nowhere.

Confirmation that Everton are not getting Kenny Tete from Fulham until they can sort out Andrei Ratiu from Rayo Vallecano [ TeamTalk ].

Galatasaray winger Barış Alper Yılmaz has been linked with us before, but here's his name again.

Everton's name keeps popping up for some surprise players – Mandela Keita, a central defensive midfielder.

Right back options out there getting very, very thin. Newly-promoted Hull City have moved for Genoa's Brooke Norton-Cuffy, another one of Everton's fullback targets this summer.

Looks like Richarlison will not be returning to Merseyside after all.

Nathan Patterson is finally going to be free. The right back is heading to Torino for a medical today ahead of a permanent transfer, leaving Vitaliy Mykolenko as the sole specialist fullback in the entire squad. Shameful.

The transfer fee is in the seven digits as can be expected, but interestingly enough, Everton have been able to put in a 30% sell-on fee clause as well.

Alan Myers is already in position bright and early on a sunny day at Finch Farm.

Welcome to RBM's transfer deadline day live blog where we'll be keeping you posted on all the latest news and rumours on this tracker, with separate detailed pieces as we get more solid confirmations.

Late last night the status was that Iliman Ndiaye was heading to Manchester City, Beto to Fiorentina and Tim Iroegbunam to Hull City – those moves should all be confirmed today. There might yet be another outgoing, we'll see – Nathan Patterson still needs a home, and West Ham want Michael Keane . A sale of Jake O'Brien has previously been mentioned too.

Jack Grealish was coming to the Blues on loan from City with a medical scheduled for this morning. Folarin Balogun should be good to go too with Everton and Monaco having reached a formal agreement yesterday evening.

Richarlison remains up in the air because a Turkish club had supposedly come in with a bigger bid for the player than Everton's offer and Spurs could be leaning that way despite the Brazilian pleading to come back to Merseyside. Kenny Tete could fall through again because Fulham are being blocked in their bid to sign his replacement. Melvin Bard had been linked as a backup left back some time ago, but that front has been quiet.

There was a late bid last night for German international winger Jamie Leweling that was rejected by Stuttgart.

Everton will likely use up one of their two domestic loan slots with Grealish, but we haven't heard anything else on any other players coming in on loan.

Transferred – Dwight McNeil (Crystal Palace)

Released – Idrissa Gueye (Al Diriyah – Saudi Pro League), Seamus Coleman (free agent), Tyler Onyango (Sheffield Wednesday)

Transferred – Hayden Hackney (Middlesbrough), Tyrique George (Chelsea), Merlin Rohl (Freiburg), Christian Norgaard (Arsenal), Brennan Johnson (Crystal Palace)

What time does the transfer window close?

The summer transfer window closes on Tuesday, Sept. 1, at 11 p.m. UK (6 p.m. ET / 3 p.m. PT) , with an additional two hour period for clubs who have already submitted deal sheets in time. This is the more traditional closing time, after the last two summer windows shut at 7pm.

Spain's La Liga's window closes at midnight, with Italy's Serie A, Germany's Bundesliga and France's Ligue 1 all at 8pm (all times UK). After the deadline no more incoming deals will be allowed, though sales of players to countries that still have transfer windows open is allowed.

Sky Sports News will be covering it all starting at 6am BST (1am EST, 10pm PST), here's info from their website on how to watch . Fans in the US will be able to follow the Sky Sports feed on the Peacock app . starting at 10am EST (5am PST).

This being the Social Media Age, follow us on Twitter where we'll be bringing you up-to-date information as we see it. Like the last couple of years, we'll be maintaining this live tracker on the website as well for you to stay updated.

articles.title: Ibrahim Mbaye: Aston Villa confirm signing of 18-year-old Paris Saint-Germain forward
articles.summary: Aston Villa have completed the signing of Paris Saint-Germain winger Ibrahim Mbaye; the 18-year-old right-sided forward has moved to Villa Park in a deal worth £47m
articles.body:
Sky Sports News understands the deal is worth £47m for the 18-year-old right winger.

The Senegal international, who scored at last summer's World Cup, was part of the PSG squad which won successive Champions League titles, as well as Ligue 1, in 2025 and 2026.

Mbaye's arrival follows the sale of England forward Ollie Watkins to Saudi Pro League side Al Hilal in a £51m transfer.

Meanwhile, Taylor Harwood-Bellis , 24, is also having a medical at Villa Park.

Villa have agreed a £30m package with Southampton to sign the England international centre-back.

The deal is broken up into a £25m guaranteed fee, plus £5m in add-ons.

Sky Sports News' Kirsty Edwards at Villa Park:

"Fast and fearless - that's how Aston Villa are describing their latest signing Ibrahim Mbaye.

"We saw him sitting in the stands last night watching Aston Villa take on Arsenal at Villa Park.

"It's over the line and it is official - Aston Villa have signed the 18-year-old from PSG in a deal worth around £47m."

Youngest African to score at the World Cup

Mbaye, 18, who primarily plays on the right wing, has come through the PSG youth system and made his debut in August 2024 as a 16-year-old.

The teenager is a Senegal international, making his bow in November 2025, having previously represented France at youth level.

Mbaye made history at the 2026 World Cup when he became the youngest African to score in the tournament, aged 18 years and 143 days old, in Senegal's 3-1 loss to France.

articles.summary: Oviedo, Almería, Mallorca y Leganés, entre sus opciones
articles.body: Uno de los nombres en los que trabaja el Atlético para aligerar su plantilla es el de Carlos Martín. El canterano está en la rampa de salida y la opción de marcharse a préstamo a un Primera división se complica... Y es ahí donde han aparecido varios de Segunda para acabar siendo su destino. Entre las opciones que se manejan para que el jugador siga su carrera esta temporada están Oviedo, Almería, Mallorca y Leganés. Son cuatro de los equipos que han preguntado a la Dirección deportiva rojiblanca para hacerse con una cesión de un jugador que el año pasado se marchó al Rayo en el mercado de enero tras no disponer de opciones durante la primera parte de la temporada. Todos ellos son equipos que se esperan que estén en la parte alta de una Segunda división que parece ser, si se llega a un acuerdo en estas horas, el destino final de un jugador que está entre los elegidos para salir en estas últimas horas de mercado.

articles.title: Tagliafico entra con fuerza en el casting del 3
articles.standfirst: El Atlético aprieta para lograr la cesión del argentino, al que el Olyimpique de Lyon le abre las puertas y al que también quiere la Juventus
articles.summary: El Atlético aprieta para lograr la cesión del argentino, al que el Olyimpique de Lyon le abre las puertas y al que también quiere la Juventus
articles.body: Nicolás Tagliafico, campeón del mundo con Argentina, entra con fuerza en el casting que Mateu Alemany lleva a cabo para fichar a un lateral izquierdo en el último día del mercado. De hecho, el director de fútbol rojiblanco trata de hacer encaje del salario del experimentado defensa de 34 años, al que el Olympique de Lyon abre las puertas y por el que también puja la Juventus. Precisamente el salario de Tagliafico en el club francés, que no atraviesa una situación económica boyante, es lo que empuja a su salida en este mercado. Una rendija por la que trata de colarse el Atlético, lanzado a por su fichaje en forma de cesión. En este sentido, en el Metropolitano hacen cuentas para tratar de acomodar sus emolumentos al ajustado límite salarial. En paralelo, Alemany continúa en su propósito de seguir agilizando las salidas de Giménez, Lemar, Carlos Martín y Obed Vargas, lo que ayudaría notablemente a cuadrar la incorporación de Tagliafico, dispuesto a priorizar al Atlético sobre el interés de la Juventus. Así las cosas, si todas las operaciones previstas en la hoja de ruta de Mateu se acaban alineando, Tagliafico sería el lateral izquierdo elegido, manteniéndose Hugo Bueno en la recámara como la opción de bajo coste. Sea como sea, Grimaldo contará con un competidor en el lateral izquierdo, tal y como adelantaría MARCA a primera hora de este intenso último día de mercado.
